title: Outstanding Room - Incredible Value
text: The hotel and staff are incredible, the room exceeded all of my expectations - this is what i would expect from something twice the rate i am paying - my only frustration has been the rudeness of other guests, parents letting their children run up and down the hallways screaming etc, you may want to bring earplugs.

title: Good hotel
text: We had good access for our family, good price. Looks clean and healthy inside. It has great convenient location. We came back to stay again. Shame I haven't booked this one for 2016, as I booked another one more expensive and quality was terrible!!!

title: Warm, caring staff at the Wellington
text: I recently went on a solo trip to London from the US, and stayed at The Wellington for 3 nights. On my first night, I was taken with extreme vertigo, and had to be transported to the hospital via ambulance. I was sick, scared, and alone in a foreign country. The staff at the Wellington could not have been more incredible. They made me feel safe and cared for. They checked on me constantly, and even went to the pharmacy to buy me medicine when I was unable to get out of bed. I will never forget the kindness, warmth, and compassion they showed me during my stay. I am forever grateful.

title: Simple, clean, straightforward, convenient
text: I have stayed in lots of hotels near Paddington station (connecting to early flights, or when I have missed the last train). Most have been horrible. As bad as any I have stayed in beyond student hostel. PILGRM (why the odd spelling?) an exception. It is not glamorous and has minimal functionality, but nothing wrong with that. It is simple, clean, straightforward - everything I want from a hotel. Staff were friendly & helpful. It is very convenient for the station. It is a bit of a labyrinth - my room was quiet but I expect some will be noisy It was very reasonably priced (though of course prices always vary)

title: Value for money hotel in a great location
text: Stayed here for one night. What I liked most about this hotel was its location. It is very near to Earl's court metro station (which has elevators - so no worries about baggage!), from which you have easy and cheap access to London Heathrow Airport (This metro station is on the Piccadilly line and since it's just outside the busiest sections of Piccadilly line, you dont have to bother much about carrying your luggage in metro - something which I consider as important!). Most tourist parts of the city are also easily accessible by metro or bus. The famous natural history museum can also be reached by foot. There are also many fast food restaurants nearby. Though small, my room was comfortable (in spite of the fact that my room was in the basement!) and had a reasonably comfortable bed. Both the room and the attached toilet were also very clean. Breakfast was also okay, though not excellent. They also have luggage storage, which I could use on the check out day. I must also mention the negatives: There was a strange smell of pesticide in the corridors (but no smell inside the rooms!). To avoid people taking key outside, they have put long and heavy threads as key chains. It was very uncomfortable and strange to carry that to breakfast halls. If loosing keys are the concern, the proprietors could easily address that problem by shifting to electronic entry modes. In spite of the minor negative aspects mentioned above, I will say that for the price I paid, it was a value for money deal and I would certainly consider it for my future stays also.

title: For people on a budget
text: I choose this hotel based on other reviews I read on Trip Advisor. When we arrived at the hotel we were given a room at the lower ground, which scared us a bit, because we imagined that it would be dark. We were relieved to find that the room was not that bad at all. We asked at the front desk if there was another room available, they said that probably on the following days we could move to another room, but we got used to it and never changed. Actually, having a room on the lower ground had its advantages: it was closer to the breakfast room and to toilets we could use. They asked us if we wanted to pay for all the nights we had booked when we arrived and hadn't even unpacked, but we chose to pay only at the end of our stay. I found this attitude a bit unpleasant. We booked a twin room, but the room we stayed in looked like a single room where another bed was added. This other bed was simply not as comfortable as the "main" bed. I found the place very clean and the staff polite. Near the hotel you have the Earl's Court station that can take you directly to the main attractions in London, without having to change lines. Yes, you can hear noise from the trains at the hotel, so if you are easily disturbed by this, don't stay there. For me it was a bit of a problem because I could only rest when the trains stopped (half past midnight), but for the other person that I travelled with this was not an issue at all. The toilets are very small... I managed to use the shower, even though I am above my ideal weight. Perhaps the toilet is the most negative point on this hotel. The area is safe and full of tourists. You have several restaurants on the main street and also supermarkets for all your needs. If you want to avoid the line at the breakfast room arrive there before 8:20. When we were leaving for our day out in London, we noticed that it was around this time that a line began to form.

title: very happy with selection
text: I only thing I was unhappy with happend only once. I wanted to end the night with a glass of wine. When I got to hotel there was a private booking in the hotel lounge abd I was denied entry. I wish they would not promote facilities that may or may not be available to guests.

title: Great location
text: We only stayed one night in an ensuite room, it was ok & met our needs for the night. We were on a budget but getting our bags up the stairs was painful but the location made up for anything else & the staff were more than helpful.

title: Delightful Stay, Minus the Construction
text: Number Sixteen is an intimate, quirkily designed boutique hotel tucked away on a quiet side street of the ideally located South Kensington. Each room has a ton of character and yet all the modern finishes you need from a luxury boutique hotel. The public spaces are similarly stylish and welcoming, and the staff is friendly and accommodating. My only complaint is that there were renovations, inside (changing the wallpaper) and outside (some sort of scaffolding) that were incredibly disruptive starting from around 8 am. There was no notice of this construction on their website, and I found it particularly irritating since I was on a conference call and could not escape the incessant banging noises and reverberations. The staff handled my complaints professionally, but I do think it's a matter of courtesy to notify guests in advance of their construction plans. I would gladly return but would have to call ahead of time to inquire about any expected noise.

title: Overall pretty good
text: Myself and my husband stayed here for 3 nights. He was doing Ride London, and after some confusion over where we were allowed to store the bike overall we had a fairly comfortable stay. There are however a few niggles: 1) We were staying in room 509. The room had a very effective air conditioning system But when I woke up in the morning, my chest was hurting and my throat was very dry. You weren’t allowed to open the window for health and safety reasons but feeling ill every morning like this just ruined my mornings. 2: The bed was comfortable but very soft so if you get a bad back, this might not help! 3: breakfast- there is a breakfast buffet included in the price and there is a lot of choice however all the cereals are very sweet, and although they said you can ask for no added sugar muesli, at the times we went for breakfast, no one was around to ask. I also think they need to be a bit strict as there were some very greedy people, one bloke had a cooked breakfast, pot of porridge, 3 pieces of toast, 4 oranges, 3 crioissants, 4 bananas, a bowel of cereal, and yoghurt and berries JUST FOR HIMSELF! Fair enough you can go and help yourself but there should be a limit I think. A lot of people stay here.. and it’s completely selfish. For what we needed it was ok, but I have stayed in better places.

title: Perfect...
text: I am going to start off this review with my only complaint... It's that I have to write a review!! I really want to keep this gorgeous hotel a secret from everyone else... And enjoy it, selfishly, for whenever I want to treat myself! My partner and I booked this hotel in the lovely Chelsea area of London as a Christmas/Late Valentines present for ourselves. I can't remember how we came to find out about it, so I will just put it down to fate and fortune. We were greeted with a beautiful front facade which was looking onto a narrow London side street, it was full of character and once inside.. The grandiose yet homely interior was just so nice, we sat next to a roaring fire as we were swiftly checked into our room by our friendly host. The family run nature of this hotel was evident, as polite children played around in what seemed like their family home, family being a strong word for this hotel. We were shown to our room, up high on the third floor... In an elevator... Up some stairs and then down some stairs... Through a narrow corridor... Some people could find this hassle, we found it amazing and just added to the experience and character even more so.. Our room door opened and we were just so happy with what was in front on us. We had booked out a double deluxe room, with a balcony. The bed was clean and the linen was crisp and well tended to. The bathroom, yet quite small, was perfect. Black marbled surfaces worked well with the White floors and furnishings and kept in tune with the vintage theme of the building and rooms. The room had everything you'd want and expect, with gorgeous furnishings well placed, old pictures hung from the walls (which were sloping inwards, just another quirky feature of this old beautiful building) a small table in the centre had a plate full of grapes and a letter welcoming us to our room. We plonked our bags down and took some pictures, before going out to the balcony to take in the lovely view of the Chelsea rooftops, the buzz of London could be felt... But wasn't overwhelming. We ordered some champagne to the room and enjoyed a few hours of leisure before heading out for dinner. We arrived back late and we were still greeted with a smile, more drinks were ordered to the room and we took in some more of the fantastic balcony views... This time the London skyline lit up the horizon. We slept like royalty and woke up to our breakfast, which we had ordered to our room! We put on our San Domenico Robes and Slippers and basked in the crisp February morning sun, once again, on the balcony. Croissants and preserves went down a treat with some tea, coffee and juices. Check out was at 12, so it was lovely to spend the morning relaxing before we had to leave. Check out was swift and again done with a smile. Credit must go to the staff, all were so kind and polite... And none of them ever seemed like employees, they did just appear to be a part of a great working family that enjoyed and took pride in their jobs. This place is going to be our come to place for a stay in London whenever we treat ourselves. If you're thinking of booking a room... Don't ask for 404... It's mine!! 10/10 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

title: Ibis Earls Court
text: Rooms were quite small and basic. Room only had one light switch which meant when going to the bathroom you had to switch on all of the lights! This was a nightmare during the night! TV was state of the art wish this could of been said for the poor quality hairdryer!

title: Close to Oxford Street
text: Chose this hotel due to it's close proximity to Oxford Street, Regent Street, Hyde Park and the West End of London. We have stayed here before and weren't disappointed. If you don't mind walking it is easy to get to Regent Street, Piccadilly, Kensington, Covent Garden... Otherwise there a number of underground stations in Oxford Street.

title: my opinion
text: Huttons hotel, i read the reviews and was scared , but my expreiance was different we booked a triple room it was on the ground floor,three single beds i speciffically askd for 3 adult beds as i didnt want to end up in a small bed for childern only , not enough power plugs for 3 ppl wanting to charge phones. complmentary tea and coffee

title: Lovely clean hotel, fab location
text: Stayed here for 4 nights in June 2018. We usually stay on Belgrave Road whenever we come to London but the cleanliness of the hotel where we normally stay has recently dipped significantly. Booked here in the hope that it would be clean if nothing else. We were not disappointed in the slightest, in fact of all the hotels we have stayed at on Belgrave Road (6 including here) this is by far the best. The hotel itself was very clean, bright and modern. The reception staff were pleasant, and although we did have to wait a couple of times for someone this was a matter of seconds rather than minutes. The lift is very slow, but it’s a very old building so it wasn’t too much of a problem. Our room (floor 4) while small (we already knew it would be) had everything we needed - a bed, kettle and a small TV. The bathroom was ample size and there was enough room to dry and get dressed without having to stand in the shower whilst doing so! The room was cleaned/tidied every day. The only negative for me would be the mattress, it sagged very badly on one side, which caused me some back pain on the first night, fortunately I was able to swop with my friend who can sleep anywhere! Breakfast was simple but filling enough. I particularly liked the porridge which I thought was lovely and creamy. Yes there are people who push and shove, and don’t understand queues or waiting, but that is no fault of the staff or the hotel. The location of the hotel is fab, 5-10 min walk to Victoria, and 5 min walk to Pimlico. Bus stop is directly opposite and takes you past Westminster, Trafalgar and down towards Oxford St. There is a luggage room which is locked where we were able to leave our bags on the last day, which is always a lovely extra. We will most definitely be staying here on our next trip to London.

title: fantastic value for money with great views
text: we (myself , 3 teenagers and a child ) stayed at the hanover hotel for one night in may whilst visiting the sights and the theatre . after reading some not so good reviews i was unsure of what to expect!! i had nothing to worry about the hotel was decorated very tastefully and the room was plenty ample , with clean sheets and towels, complimentry tea and coffee and even freeview to the boys delight ! the bathroom was compact but clean and ample , even for my 6.5ft brother ! the views at night were fantastic looking out onto a floodlit houses of parliment and london eye (room 27) . breakfast was served up until 9.30 which is ideal when your not such an early riser , with as much tea ,coffee ,juice ,toast and preserves as you can eat , along with a full english or cereal . everyone at breakfast was tucking in and i saw no complaints . We were able to leave our bags in a left luggage room until later on the day of departure giving us another days shopping without carrying the bags with us . the staff were friendly and accomodating . if you want imacculate accomodation with five star service then this isnt for you .(and will cost you far more in this location ) if you want extremely reasonable rates with comfortable rooms clean sheets and a more than ample breakfast , close to londons attractions then i highly rercomend the hanover . it was a fantastic experience and will be booking again when we return to london .

title: luxury apartment in a heart of London
text: stayed here in May with big families. Got an upgrade for one bedroom suite which is lovely. the bed was quite comfortable, the furniture is well maintained even though some of them looked quite old. there are some construction work undergoing, therefore the lift is not working and we have to use the service lift which was very uncomfortable. one of other guest that it has not been fixed since one month. hopefully it is completed right now. Location, in the heart of London. 10 minutes walking to tube station and bus station. quiet and posh area. didnt try the breakfast, because quite expensive compare to other's. i would recommend to stay here if you can get reasonable price!

title: Haven of Peace !
text: Ideally situated just off Hyde and Green Park the Mews is an ideal place to stay with easy access by foot to many places including Buckingham Palace a mere 10 mins at most . The staff are very customer focused , the rooms are comfortable and all is quiet . I hate to finish on a low note but ...........our only disappointment was breakfast with the staff not particularly interested - the food offering was bland , tasteless with scrambled eggs inedible + if you want smoked salmon its an extra £10.00 .......no way !

title: Simply you get what you pay for!
text: I stayed at the Prince William a while ago! They're now under the renovation which is clearly posted on every website! You have to check in at the opposite hotel and breakfast which is free of charge is served at the same hotel. The room was spotless comfortable beds and amazing bathroom and toilet in the room plus a huge flat screen TV with coffee and tea facilities. Average room sizes for a hotel in central London. I see so many of travelers complain about simple stuff, checking is after 3pm then why do you think stuff is rude by telling you that rooms are not yet ready if you arrive before 3pm. so many horrible reviews I was so curious to see the reality of what's written here but surprisingly most of them were not true! There is no lift at the moment but a kind porter available to help you with your luggage. In general cheap and the location is the middle of London close to few stations and many buses available just minutes walk from where the hotel is based! Let's not forget the free WiFi available in the room without paying a penny for which isn't usual in most of the hotels in London. would definitely stay again and I strongly recommend it.

title: Great location
text: Close toEarls court station and close to main strip. Rooms was clean, bathroom rather small when getting out of shower need to have to door open bit of a squeeze. Breakfast was very bland and the only hot food was toast and boiled eggs. Very small room so you have to get there at the right time otherwise you have to wait. Four at a table is very small. No tea coffee making facilities in the room only in the lounge.

title: Okay for a short stay
text: Stayed here for one night whilst sightseeing. On arrival it was good. The staff were nice and efficient and shown us to our room. The room was nice. Has everything we needed for the night, tea, coffee, towels, soap, shampoo, conditioner, tv. Our main problem was the noise from outside! I understand it's not going to be quiet given its location but we had a fairly sleepless night due to the noise coming through the windows! And draft! The windows are terrible and need replacing!!!!

title: Nice pub B&B
text: Got to say that when the taxi pulled up we were a little worried but this is a London Pub with B&B rooms above so don't be as surprised as we were! However, you're made to feel really welcome and the rooms are clean and tidy. I feel that if you get a comfortable nights sleep then it's worth the money you pay and that's exactly what we all got. Yes it's in the middle of a housing estate and clearly it's a good local for a number of people. We stayed on a Saturday and karaoke was on but we didn't hear a pep. When we arrived we were welcomed nicely and made to feel like we were locals anyway. When I went down for a beer, everyone was welcoming and chatty. In summary a bit like the Old Vic of the telly but that actually made it nicer than a chain hotel.

title: Fab location and friendly staff
text: I have just stayed at the Admiral Hotel, after being recommended here from a friend. I felt compelled to write a review after seeing all those reviews from those of you who haven't even stayed and wrote terrible reviews based on the C4 programme! When I checked in I was greeted by both Kevin and So, who were both very hospitable, and even offered to help with our bags as we were struggling a little. Kevin was extremely polite and went through a few things to do in London, walking distances to local attractions etc. I must also say the photos really don't do it justice! We were given a recently refurbished room, silver wallpaper, USB plug sockets, and comfy sheets. We also booked in for £260 for a triple room with a lovely view over the weekend,which worked out at £40 pp, much lower than advertised on four in a bed! Not sure why it was advertised at that price. 🤔 Would recommend and will be back for Winter Wonderland! 😀

title: Spot on!
text: I decided at the last minute (2 days notice) to take my girlfriend to london for a couple of days for her birthday. Going to watch a show in leicester square I needed to find somewhere near by on a reasonable budget as I'd rather spend the money on her than somewhere to sleep! At £69 for the night with a continental breakfast the grange white hall was one of the cheapest and pretty close to where we needed to be. Spending this amount in this location was a bit of a worry but we were both pleasantly surpised at the room, service and breakfast, all spot on!!! Would highly recomend at twice the price!!

title: Overnight delight
text: We could not fault our recent overnight stay at this hotel from reception to breakfast all first class, except for the teapot poured badly! There was even a choice of pillows and the hotel is so local for the West End.we would go there again

title: Great Location but poor WIFI
text: We stayed at Park Avenue, Belgravia for 7 nights in early August. We got the room at a good rate which is definitely not the norm for this part of town. I think all the hotels dropped their prices significantly after the Olympics began as they realised the expected vacancy rates were not coming to fruition. After our flight arrived from Australia in the early morning, we attempted to check in early however the room was not available. We were however give some face towels and a toilet with basin to freshen up before leaving our bags and departing for the day. The best thing about this hotel is the location and it's proximity to Victoria rail, tube and bus stations. It is also 10 mins walking distance to Buckingham Palace and The Mall. Breakfast was nice, however after a few days straight it does tend to get a little boring. The WIFI was horrible, we were on the second floor and it was in and out for the whole week which made it extremely frustrating to use. All in all it was a nice hotel in a great location.

title: Good Hotel and Location
text: The Cons: 1- I called the hotel 2 times on two different occasions to confirm our arrival and make some request. The hotel failed to notify me, even though I am a Hilton Honors member with gold status, either on the two occasions I called the hotel, or by email or text, that this area of the city will host a bicycle race and that all limousine and taxi access to the hotel will not be possible. As a result, myself and my family had to be dropped at a subway station with 5 pieces of large luggage to take the subway to a station near the hotel. We had to carry our luggage up and down the stations and walk the streets to the hotel. This is really unacceptable and the hotel should have informed their arriving guests of this event and offer them options. 2- The Junior suite we stayed in was very small in comparison to other junior suites in other properties I previously stayed in when in London. 3- On our first night, a trailer was dropping merchandise on the street our room is overlooking. The driver kept the engine on and it was extremely loud and we were unable to sleep. I called the front desk and they acknowledged the issue and said that they cannot do anything about it and it will take some time. Pros

title: A Little calm place in London
text: We had a two night stay here while visiting family in East Sheen. The rooms are tastefully decorated and there are some nice touches - there's a fridge downstairs in the accommodation area where you can help yourself to a complimentary bottle of still or sparkling water, also a tray to brew your own tea or coffee. This meant fresh milk rather than horrid little plastic tubs! Breakfast is served in the conservatory - plentiful newspapers. Tea, coffee & fresh juice are served, otherwise it's help yourself. Nothing exciting, but fine. We had an evening meal for the family one night. We thought it was a touch expensive (London prices!) and that the choice for our veggie daughter was limited (Only one main course, which she could have made any day) The kitchen were asked if there was anything else they could do, but no they couldn't. That's a bit disappointing & we pointed it out to the staff, who accepted the feedback well and said they'd take it on board. This is, after all, a gastropub with rooms rather than an hotel. We liked the ambience and overall, we'd stay again

title: Great location and Great value
text: I stayed here recently for an overnight, between business and personal commitments. This comes up fairly often, so I have tried out hostels, pod rooms, airbnbs, several hotels, before finding Pasha. I found this to be the best value/quality/location/price combo for me. The room was clean, comfortable and warm. It had tea and coffee facilities and a large bathroom. It was quiet. The staff were friendly and offered to help me with bags. There's a busy bus route a 2 minute walk away, making it cheap and easy to get around London. For the first time in months, I have booked the same place back-to-back stays because I think I've finally found a hotel that is cheap, without being dirty/sketchy/having terrible facilities or suchlike!

title: Conveniently situated B & B
text: We spend one night with our dog at The Grange it was a cosy enough room with a very small en suite bathroom. The bed was cosy and clean but unfortunately the window would only open with slat bits in it at the top one side and we were amazingly hot even though we had turned the radiator off/down. Luckily enough there was a fan in the wardrobe so we could calm and cool the dog down, he has a bad heart and was getting himself into a terrible state! Our bedroom was at the back of the house so was quite quiet we liked watching the squirrel and birds out of the window in the morning. Our bedroom door was very warped so could do with replacing. It was basic but upto London standards good we had a single and a double bed in our room. Breakfast was good, yoghurt, cereal, a bowl of fruit, cooked breakfast, toast, tea or coffee. It set us up for the day. We had only came to visit Kew Gardens to see the orchids and left our dog with a sitter from DogBuddy. The lady who greeted us was very friendly and gave us info on the bus - they only accept contactless card and oyster card by the way NO cash. The cats Boots is lovely and I so wanted to take him home in my handbag!

title: pleasantly suprised
text: After reading the reviews I was resigned to a terrible stay BUT was pleasantly suprised. The hotel has obviously just been renovated and was fresh and clean looking. The lobby was very classy and the rooms very tidy. Beds comfy, lovely fresh linen and plenty of space. The bathroom smelt awful and the window didnt do up, but those were minor compared to what we were expecting! For a budget hotel it was great. Great location, friendly staff and even breakfast provided. Will stay again.

title: Great hostel good place to start london adventure
text: We stayed here for a few weeks while looking for a house/Jobs and its the best hostel we have stayed in through out Europe. Its clean, showers are decent, mattresses are comfy, theres good sized cages under the beds to lock ur whole backpack and not have to worry about your stuff and you get free breakfast!!! as well as good deals in the belushis bar below. Close as to heaps of shops and tube and All the staff were super friendly and helpful would recommend to all :)

title: Solid budget option - easy access to centre
text: For the price this is a decent option. Short walk to dlr which takes you into town centre very quickly. Also shops near the dlr including a Tesco, a decent Turkish restaurant and a craft beer pub. Room was actually quite quiet despite being on the busiest road in London. Only criticism I have is the service at reception/bar was very slow in the evenings. Watching the older European lady use the reception computer reminded me of watching my grandma use a computer for the first time. Painful!

title: Small friendly hotel
text: The Gateway is situated on the busy A24 on Balham Hill, London. It is within easy walking distance of the Northern Line tube station, Balham Station and the town of Balham itself. Do not expect any frills but do expect a very warm welcome. The hotel has two parts, the older original property and an added new extension. We were accomodated in the older side. The room and bathroom was clean and of a reasonable size. There are tea/coffee facilities and a television. Room 6 was facing the road and did suffer from some road noise, however the hotel provides earplugs - I slept soundly in the comfortable bed. Car parking is very limited so you need to book a space in advance. Entry is by way of a large metal gate, I suggest you telephone ahead when you are near the hotel and ask them to open the gate as there is no parking nearby and access is difficult due to the busy road. I recommend this clean friendly hotel for people who require easy access to London and do not wish to pay the extortionate prices charged by more up-market hotels in the area.

title: An excellent budget option ...
text: A group of us (two couples) stayed here recently. For London the rooms were a good size and clean. The staff were also helpful. It is about 200m from the tube (northern line) for sightseeing and close to Clapham High St for nights out. For anyone who doesn't want to pay extortionate prices in the city centre I would definately recommend this hotel!

title: IT'S ALL ABOUT VALUE FOR MONEY!!
text: My wife & I have stayed at The New Inn on two occasions after using very expensive city centre London hotels and would in future always stay at the New Inn. Let’s be honest from the start, the New Inn is no fancy boutique B&B charging £200+ a night. It’s a very clean basic place that offers the traveller on a budget a decent room for the night. For me a B&B has to offer three things

title: On balance, good value stay in a good location
text: There are thousands of 'budget' places like this in London, ranging from really terrible to pretty good. I've stayed in all kinds.The Bloomsbury Palace is at the higher end of the scale. I booked a single room, which admittedly was one of the smallest I've ever stayed in. But it was clean (recently refurbished), the bed was comfortable and the bathroom had plenty of hot water, towels and other essentials. Wifi was free and worked perfectly. There was even free tea, coffee and biscuits. No wardrobe, just a rail to hang things, but nothing to complain about unless you're the cat -swinging type. It was very noisy at night (room 106 is at the front of the building on the first floor, and Gower Street is busy all night.) But it's Central London - what do you expect? With a bus stop across the street, offering regular buses to the West End, and Goodge Street tube 5 mins walk away, it's well connected. Plenty of coffee shops, restaurants, pubs, shops nearby. The breakfast was freshly cooked and a pretty good Full English it was too - served by friendly and smiley staff. Finding a place to stay down town without paying an arm and two legs is never easy. This place was a pretty good compromise, and I will probably use it again.

title: Long Weekend Away
text: Pre-med students came to London for a long weekend to sit our GAMSAT exam. Had a great stay, nice facilities and the hotel staff are very friendly and helpful. Saad is a top guy- great to banter with and made our stay a laugh! Great value, perfect place to crash if you're planning a busy weekend.

title: Excellent service. Beautifully appointed modern rooms.
text: We received excellent service upon checking and throughout our 24 hour stay. The room is well designed with amazing linens and mattress, great body products, and well designed and spacious modern room. Great location, and wonderful food assortments. Great staff. Had a lovely vibe. Only negative was whomever I spoke to when making a reservation was extremely rude. Maybe a tad overpriced as well. The place is super clean and refreshing.

title: Dont see the problem!
text: Well after reading the other reviews its safe i was terrified about staying here.... Couple of days trip away with my Mum, Auntie and Granny who i knew would not be impressed if all these reviews were the case. However we arrived slightly early and for a £10 charge got checked into the room as it was ready. With baited breath we headed up the stairs, which is quite a thin, steep staircase. The guy at reception showed us around the room and we took a sigh of relief... although it was quirky, it was clean and had all the facilities we needed. Shower gel and shampoo provided along with clean towels and all the things we needed in the kitchen, which was basically mugs for the morning and wine glasses for the evening. For all the time we spent in the apartment as were always out and about, it was exactly what we needed. High table with four chairs to chill and talk around in the late evenings and then off to bed, which i need need to climb over the beams to get to my bed, which i more found funny than anything else but probably not ideal for an older crowd. Upstairs there were three beds and air conditioning which we did use. The street noise you could hear but when the clock struck one it went peaceful very quickly. So many places to eat and drink right at your doorstep and a two minute walk from the underground. Was ideal for us and exactly what we needed. Would 100% go back and stay again.

title: Check in very disappointed
text: Upon arrival, we were a little early, 45 mins, told to go away and come back in 45 min time, after doing so we came back and there made to wait like school children until our room was ready, customer service was very unfriendly, won’t be staying there again.

title: Worth every penny
text: Just got back from a 2 day stay here and I can't speak more highly about it. If you are travelling as a family don't waste time with hotels stay here. Only a 5 minute walk from Greenwich and all the travel links into London you could want. My only issues would being new it can be a bit hard to find,also there is still building work going on so if your a light sleeper a 8 o'clock wake up call might be a bit annoying, but as we were on the 12th floor it wasn't a problem.

title: Family of five
text: If you are looking for a place to lay your head while doing a whirlwind tour of London with three kids and not much money, this is the place for you! We just wanted a roof over our heads, and a bed to sleep in, and thats what we got. The decor was not a factor for us, we got the family room which had its own adequate ensuite, with plenty of hot water. The beds were comfy and clean, and the TV worked. Breakfast was prompt, and had handy snack packs and juice boxes which we took with us on our sightseeing. The concierge Martin was fantastic. If you are looking for a laundrymat, there is one on just down the road, opens from 8 to 8. Lots of restaurants, the Hop on Hop off bus is literally just on the corner, the train station is 2 minutes from the front door, the cabs cost @ 12-15 pounds to get around to Oxford St, Notting Hill, Harrods, Kings Cross. The Tube was terrifying for this country Australian, but soon got used to it, unfortunately half the time it was closed!

title: Not a *5, but perfect in other ways.
text: Hotels in London don't come a lot cheaper than they do at Her Majesty. And if they do, they're tiny and often lacking in basic amenities (like hot water) at best--or absolutely decrepit at worst. Actually, the same can be said of many much more expensive hotels as well. Thus, I was shocked at the cleanliness and size of the rooms at Her Majesty. No one ever pretended it was 5 star quality, but the owner strives hard to make sure that what you do get is spotless and comfortable. I'm not sure there's a better bargain in town honestly. The only negative, IMO, is the location. Shepard's Bush Green is fine, but it is a little bit outside of many of the areas that us non-Londoners want to frequent when we come to stay in the city. However, it does have easy access to the tube (2 stations within 2 or 3 blocks--Shepard's Bush on the central line and Shepard's Bush Market on the Circle & Hammersmith and City lines... all zone 2), so central London isn't more than about 15 minutes away. Overall, if you're looking for a cheap, no frills London getaway that is immaculately clean with lots of comfort for value, this is a great option.

title: Basic, clean, but expensive!
text: Very basic for the cost, but very clean and the staff were very polite. I am sure if we had looked harder we could have found somewhere much cheaper with a double bed and a bigger bathroom. But on the upside we found that the Marylebone Summer Fair was on that weekend and we were right in the middle of it so a bonus for our Sunday! One thing, be sure you don't travel on Gay Pride Parade Saturday, the traffic is a appalling and the cost of getting anywhere in a taxi is not good, we were sure we paid more that we should have.

title: Excellent
text: Being a regular for years after knowing one or two really awful hotels in london. This one is clean, friendly staff and even if prices can seems high, it is worthwile if you compare it to other 3 stars hotels in london..

title: Cheap and well connected
text: I found this hotel to be quiet, clean, and very well situated for access to Borough, London Bridge and Brixton - for the price. For the price I paid, sharing a bathroom is hardly an imposition, and I found the premises to be very clean given how many people were using them. Many reviewers have also taken issue with the location of the hotel. My feeling on this is simple: if you want the London of the movies, stay in Notting Hill and be prepared to pay for it. There is a bus stop right opposite the hotel with a night bus service, and therefore no reason to walk around late at night if this bothers you. I saw no evidence of "feral gangs" or any need to jump straight in a taxi. You are far more likely to be pickpocketed on Oxford Street than attacked on a hundred metres of busy, well-lit street in a multicultural part of Southwark.

title: AGAIN AND AGAIN
text: I was over in London for a weekend and decided to stay in this hotel as a result of a previous experience. Firstly hats off to the staff. As a H Gold member i was up graded to an executive room with access to the lounge. I see now why the bar closes at 21.00 it is a very different type of customer as the girls in the lounge had to put with dogs abuse on two of the nights that I was there. For some of the staff English was their 2nd language yet they must have known that they were been slagged off. yet they were very professional. I can't recommend this hotel strongly enough, very close to city airport yet only 25 mins to westminter station

title: Going back next time!
text: I and a friend were here in July 2013 for four nights. There are at least three things that are great about this hotel: 1. It is located centrally with a walking distance from Paddington subway and Train Station that can take you directly to Heathrow airport, and Oxford Street, if you come from Gatwick you can take the subway directly to Paddington from Victoria Stations who connects with the Gatwick Express and Southern line. 2. When I was there I met guest who returns every time they are in London-(3) but not only because the price is one of the best in the same area of many hotels. This B&B is run by the Norwegian, English and Burmese speaking Ally family since 1994 after living several years in Oslo, Norway (They might even know some more languages that I did not ask for) as my mother tongue is Norwegian I did all my communication in Norwegian with them without any problems at all. I will definitely recommend this hotel if you are Scandinavian speaking and do not feel comfortable with your English or if just want a “laid back” chat after a long day with “tourist” English in London. They even had an adaptor that connected with my Norwegian telephone charger that I had forgotten at home, and they have maps and information pamphlets for free. The double room we got was cosy, very clean, had tee-and coffee making facilities and TV. Even in the summer you can choose between the regular sheets and a fluffier sheet to cover yourself with at night, which is great for me who tends to freeze even in the summer (most hotels I have gone to do not provide fluffy sheets in the summer). The breakfast was nice and plenty. They also got Wi -Fi Dwight and his Wife Farzana did everything to meet our needs, it really shows that they are dedicated to their business and they go far to make you feel at home so I will guarantee you will feel very welcomed here, and if there is something you are missing do not be afraid to ask them! We met Dwight’s brother Gary at their Burmese restaurant only a stone’s throw away from the hotel, the brothers run the Hotel and Restaurant together, so do not get surprised if you find them in the hotel and restaurant at the same day (The restaurant had a range of vegetarian dishes to choose from, so this is a vegetarian and vegans heaven). Next time I am in London I will not hesitate to book a room at Mandalay again, and I have already recommended it to several friends as I do not they will not get disappointed.

title: Nice but expensive
text: Apartment is Ok, spacious and clean. Location is handy, next to Trafalgar square, shops and restaurants. However, gets very crowded on rush hours and using a taxi is not that recommended. There is no staff onsite to help, need to phone for all requirements. Sofa bed was terrible for me, my son son enjoined. If travelling with young children avoid to rent the 2 floors flat as the the stairs are very tipped. Also, on the second there is only the room and a bathroom, no place for childrens basically. All properies have a touchscreen control panel to adjust loghtning, room temperature and access to the sound system.

title: Don't listen to bad reviews!
text: After booking to stay here I found lots of negative reviews so much so that I was dreading turning up here with my family! I was so relieved and pleasantly surprised when we opened the door and found a perfectly decent apartment much bigger and cleaner than expected. Nothing was old or broken as some reviews claimed and it was more than adequate for a theatre break with my partner and two boys. 2 mins walk from Kilburn Park tube station which is so handy with children after a long day of walking around! Only thing I would suggest is having a proper storage room for luggage to make you feel slightly more at ease when leaving belongings there as we had to leave ours in reception, the reception is manned 24 hrs a day so it is secure and our bags were left there all day before checking in and prior to checking out and were fine. All in all perfect stay, good service and no complaints what so ever. Would definitely stay here again :)

title: So-So So Quartier.....
text: Myself and 10 friends stayed in two apartments for a hen party. First impressions were nice modern spacious apartments but both had hideous rotten suage smells and on close inspection were quite dirty and obviously uncleaned from the previous guests. Once we'd overcome those issues, we were horrified to find that one apartment had no hot water!!!!!! Reception quickly sent somebody to fix it, but they couldn't....so offered us a different smaller room which was too late anyway as the hen party was in full swing. The beds were comfortable, kitchen well stocked and bathroom modern. Location good access for central London. Good price when split between a few of you....otherwise probably not.

title: Perfect location, amazing staff and great space
text: Stayed in Go Native Monument for a week on my most recent trip to London - a city notorious for small hotel rooms at an exorbitant price but this place is amazing! I stayed in a studio apartment on the ground floor, it had a well kitted out kitchen, had a small living area (sofa, TV), plus a table big enough for laptop, papers and my tea! The staff were so helpful and friendly throughout. WiFi excellent which is also important and the room incredibly quiet. In addition, the tube is not far from the apartments (2 small streets i.e. 2 min walk). It's also very easy to get to places after work (Borough just across London Bridge), Leadenhall Market (would recommend The Butchers for something to eat) by foot. So really a great find and I shall be staying here again

title: Great budget place
text: Stayed in a single room for one night with shared facilities (bathroom and kitchen) in early July, 2018. Pros: Conveniently located next to two Underground stations (Euston and Euston Square, depending on the line that you want to take) Clean shower stalls and toilets Cheap (I booked around a month beforehand and it cost me around £51) Buffet breakfast with sufficient choices Towels and basic toiletries provided Cons: Dirty stained carpet (remember to wear shoes/slippers) Window can only be opened slightly and the hot weather wasn't helping either Broken fan (only a small breeze came out from the sides!) Wifi is free but slightly slow Would recommend, especially to solo travellers.

title: Bargain Price In A Good Location.
text: We had difficulty finding it in the first place as it's just a small plaque saying LSE Passfield Hall, not in any way like a hotel sign (which it isn't of course). We were on the second floor at the back of the building so was very quiet, except that the radiator made the most horrendous noise at about midnight on our first night there. It was actually turned off and I had to turn it on to stop the noise (which was like pneumatic drill). Consequently, for the rest of our stay, we had to leave the radiator on, which did make it a bit warm in the middle of the night. The room was quite large and basic with many stains on the carpet, which was a bit off putting but I don't think it was actually dirty, probably tea and coffee stains. Knowing what to expect, we took a travel kettle and some tea and coffee so could make ourselves a drink if required, I also took a hairdryer as they aren't provided either. The toilets and showers on our floor were closed, so we had to go either up or down a flight of stairs whenever we needed to 'go' which was a bit of a bind, but even having to 'double up' with the other floors, I only saw someone else on two occasions. The breakfast is superb and really set us up for the day. There are lots of buses into the West End, and it's a steady walk to Oxford Street. An absolute bargain if you're on a budget and we will definitely stay here the next time we visit London.

title: They helped me out of a pickle!
text: I stay in London every week in business and had booked a Wednesday evening at a different Ibis. That Wednesday evening my schedule suddenly changed and I had to find a room for the following evening and selected this hotel. I quickly booked online and the next day, packed up my bag and moved hotels. I arrived to discover that I had made a huge error. In my haste, I had booked for the same day as my other hotel. This meant I didn’t have a room for the night and I had been charged in full as a ‘no show’ for the night before. I stood there in despair! I had no time to try and find anywhere else but I had nowhere to stay. Within minutes the helpful team at the hotel transferred my incorrect booking to the correct night which meant I now had somewhere to stay. They strictly didn’t need to as it was my error. They did it to help me out. Thank you for being so flexible. Many other hotels wouldn’t be.

title: Great Accommodation
text: We were here from 14 March to the 21st. It was more than what we expected. It felt like it was our own home. Facilities are new, the Kitchen and Bathroom are clean and well maintained. The apartment is secured with state-of-the-art security panels to give you a peace of mind while you're asleep. The place is walking distance from the mall and few establishments. Tube station is literally a few steps away from the apartment. We were actually sad when we left the place as it felt like home to us. Book this directly to their website to avail cheaper booking :)

title: Few good points
text: The best point of the hotel would have to be the location, with restaurants and shops just steps away, and a 5 minute walk to the tube. The decor in the rooms is very nice and modern, and the rooms are cleaned well daily. The rooms however are tiny, we had a room with two doubles and for four people there is just no room to move. The space issue is a big problem at breakfast as you have to get up very early to get a seat, the breakfast is pretty poor (its really just toast) The rooms were very hot and stuffy when we visited and it would be really helpful if they could provide a mini fridge in the room. We were surprised that we were not able to make use of a communal fridge or even get an ice bucket. This hotel is suitable as a base at the most but I don't think it is worth the price as there are better budget options about.

title: Not for me..
text: We stayed here in July for 2 nights, a quick stop before travelling on to the rest of Europe... We stayed in a private room with ensuite. The room was small and very basic, bed, drawers & rubbish bin. The bathroom was actually the better part of the room. Our room looked onto a alleyway, the second door leading onto the alleyway could not be opened and the only window we had could only be opened about 30 centimetres a security measure i think? Was very hot during the night though so we slept with the window open and it was still hot. Also there were no drapes so we were up as soon as the sun came up which didn't help with our jetlag. The breakfast is very basic but still nice that they include it. The hostel staff are really great always friendly and know quite a lot! The hostel also organises pub crawls and drinks etc but we were so tired from sightseeing all day and the jet lag so we only went to the drinks they had in the hostel. The hostel is located sort of between Gloucester Rd & South Kensington tube stations, about 10 minutes each way and Hyde Park is only just up the road. Unfortunately there are no places to really eat that are close by.. While this place might be ok for some, it was too far away for us and we'd definitely stay somewhere else next time.

title: Lovely hotel let down by the food
text: The hotel itself is lovely, large clean room with a very comfortable king sized bed. Only a 5 minute walk to an NCP car park, which is just outside of the congestion zone. My husband and I have visited Nobu restaurants in the past, which was the main reason that we stayed at this hotel, being able to order room service. The website states that you can order from the main menu shown on the website, however this is not true, and the room service menu is considerably smaller. The quality of the food here is definitely not up to par with the other Nobu restaurants. The wagyu burger sliders were raw, I think that there needs to be a warning on the menu about this, as this actually made me sick. I don’t mind paying extra money for a really good meal, but the food bill (no drinks) was over £130 for 2 of us, half of the food we couldn’t eat, and we were both left very hungry! Tried to speak to someone, was told a manager was not available and would call me back - never did. We were in a rush in the morning so just had to pay the bill and leave. £75 for the robe, although very nice just seems a bit extreme. I don’t think that we will return.

title: Can’t get there
text: Was a nice enough hotel and service was very good but having to walk due to taxis not being allowed into the zone didn’t empress the wife , how can she be expected to walk to this establishment when she’s wearing hills , also it’s in hackney which isn’t the type of area where it’s safe to walk around with its crime epidemic . 1st and definitely last visit for me

title: When was the last time you did something for the first time?
text: Very elegant - contemporary design, great location, very nice bar and great restaurant. However, the staff was very young and amateur like - from the check in to the check out. My husband and I had an issue with a room next to us where there seemed to be a party going on until 7 am (many people coming in and out throughout the night and early morning and slamming the door) which resulted in no sleep at all for both of us and the hotel stuff was unable to deal with the situation even though we made a call down the reception at 4 am and a personal visit an hour later. At the check out, I asked for operations manager, but only had a chance to talk to one of the girls at the reception whose apology was inadequate. We were offered a special care on our next visit, but assured this young lady that there was most definitely not going to be another visit to their otherwise trendy establishment.

title: Great Location – But . .
text: The hotel is a few hundred metres from the Earls Court station. But the rooms are small with even smaller shower / toilet. The room we had certainly could do with a new bed (which was up against the wall on one side). Breakfast was fine. Overall, was not impressed.

title: Lunch with friends
text: Casual lunch with friends. Food acceptable although bit on the pricey side for what it is. A quarter of rotisserie chicken including two sides around the £13 mark and the chicken was dry. Very welcoming, pleasant staff although I object to the practice of adding a £1 charitable donation on my behalf to the establishments charity of choice. If the Ship inn wish to give to charity they can do it from their profit, I prefer to chose when donating rather than it being done/ added to my bill without even asking. To clarify I do give to charity but when I chose to not when I’m eating out.

title: Great location but very small room
text: Despite the friendly staff and great location, I think this was the smallest hotel room of my life. There wasn’t even a bedside table - no room. They also resemble more a furnished apt than a hotel. There is no room for breakfast - you have to take it in your tiny small room. Not staying again. Ever.

title: Incredibly overpriced & far from a luxury or 5 star hotel!
text: I never write reviews but I felt incredibly ripped off by this hotel and wanted to warn others. The street its on is adorable, the lobby was nice enough, and the few staff members were well-meaning, but not well trained. Payment for the room was required in advance upon check-in

title: Amazed
text: I am amazed hotel management have not responded to the latest review nearly 2 weeks after it was posted. I sympathize with the poster and hope all turns out well, but it says something about the vigilance of hotel management that they don't care or are still unaware how important these reviews are to their business.

title: We wouldn't recommend this place
text: Pro's: - the location was really good, only 2 min. walk from St. Pancras / King's Cross (metro)station, cool pubs, nice coffee places and supermarkets - Real cosy roof top terrace - nice decoration in the common room Con's: - they didn't provide an adapted socket for other European plugs to charge your phone or camera so you had to buy it somewhere - the bathrooms were quite dirty with constant wet floors, hair all over the place and other dirt - The staff wasn't really helpfull and it seemed like they didn't really know how the place worked - The room was extremely tiny (for 2 people, we couldn't even stand next to eachother, the full room was 2x3 meters) - We couldn't close the window (it was stuck) so it was quite cold and really noisy from the traffic downstairs in the street - Twice we came to the common room on time to have breakfast, twice they said we couldn't have breakfast anymore without further explanation - We had to pay 2 pounds per pag after we checked out to keep our luggage safe for an hour or two (never seen before) We wouldn't recommend this place.

title: Amazing hotel, excellent staff, perfect location, shame we were sleeping in a cupboard.
text: We arrived early and our room was not ready yet, the staff dealt with us perfectly, friendly and helpful. The bar was nice and the breakfast was pretty good too. We went for the second cheapest double room, 'executive' they called it. For the money paid the location and quality of the hotel is exceptional. The room size would have been funny if it wasn't me who had to sleep there. There wasn't even enough space in the room to open our suitcase without putting it on the bed. I understand that central London

title: Minutes from Hyde Park
text: I would only stay here if I needed to be in the area. Our group found the rooms to be quite small for the price. The staff was very helpful but this facility needs some serious renovation. There are much better hotels within minutes of this place.

title: hurry up breakfast
text: Date 28 June 2007 Just returned from 3 nights at this hotel. As a 2 star hotel, the location was great:-10 mins walk from tube (Central Line) and buses. Room, as expected form other reviews, was small and bathroom tiny . Also dark . Glad it wasn't hot weather as might be stifling. Had requested a larger room but this was hardly that!!! Main complaint was about breakfast. Scheduled for 7-9am, went down at 8.50 to find only allowed 1 cup of coffee , toast that had barely winked at the toaster and to be told to 'please eat quickly' as the servers were finishing at 9 ! When I queried this, i was informed that the servers ' were only paid until 9 and had other work to do.' Needless to say, did not bother the other mornings. If you want a cheap convenient hotel, this is OK but certainly no frills and not particularly hospitable staff

title: Mmmmm - not impressed
text: def not impressed - the rooms are small and old. We were a family of 3 and falling over ourselves. The show came to pieces in our hands and we had to tie it up to get any water. The only good thing I can say is the location is fab and the breakfast delicious.

title: Haunted
text: Do not stay at this hotel I was up all night as i kept hearing strange noises coming from the doors and the bathroom. I sware there is something lurking in the small dingy corridors of this place! Nice beans tho

title: One night with our three grand children.
text: Very dated and in need of decoration. Over priced for what we paid. Not a nice experience for our grand children!!!!! Only good thing about it was its location. The whole hotel needed up dating and renovation as it was extremely run down. I would give it no stars if that was possible.

title: Rose court hotel london
text: Only for people who do t mind staying in a very simple hotel in a very simple-not recently renovated room! Besides that the location is perfect, 3 minutes walk from marble arch tube station, breakfast is simple but good.

title: The room was definitely bad
text: A room located underground, exactly under the lobby (so that each time somebody entered the hotel, I heard their steps loudly) without speaking about the toilets of the reception also located above the room and which made a huge noise each time they were used... No table nor desk (of course) A very tiny bathroom Really a bad room. Otherwise, the hotel looks nice from the outside..!

title: Very disappointing clastrophobic single room
text: Booked for 7 nights as single adult traveler. I got tiny single room, about 2*2.2m where the toilets were outside the room under the stairs. The toilets were very small, where one should have a flexibility of Chinese rubber girl in order to sit and relax there. obviously there no place for towel in the toilets. After one night (actually 12hr upon arrival) I paid a fine, and run away to different hotel.

title: Cheap and cheerful hotel in great location
text: Stayed here for 3 nights. Great base 5 mins from Marble Arch. Rooms very small but clean and warm. Bed ok Breakfast included was fine and enough to set you up for he day Staff were friendly and helpful. Fine for a budget break to London with no frills. We left the room after breakfast each morning and didn't return till bed time so didn't need anything fancy.

title: Only plus is the location
text: Spent only one night at this hotel, but that was plenty. The room was the tiniest room I have ever stayed in and the cleanliness left a lot to be desired, as did the maintenance. Thick layers of dust everywhere, the hardware around the mini sink was loose and it took a good 5 minutes to get the first warm water to flow. The location close to Marble Arch was the only good thing about this hotel.

title: Negative for extremely tight rooms, positive for location
text: Rooms: negative experience. Location: very good. Room 305 is extremely tight, derived from staircase room, almost claustrophobic. Bed is slightly more than single. No wardrobe (only three hooks). We asked to change room and were given room 404, just slightly better but toilet even smaller. Considering the price, rooms should be much better.Renewing is needed. Safebox and lift was the only positive part, together with location, about 5 minutes walk to Queensway and 8 minutes from Bayswater tube station. Breakfast was acceptable: cereals, bread, jam, honey, tea, coffee, industrial fruit salad.

title: Nice location, poor conditions
text: We made a last minute booking for 1 night stay in London and we ended up choosing the Leisure Inn due to its location. It stands near to Bayswater shopping area and tube station and a short walking distance from Hyde Park. The area around is very nice, quiet and safe to stay on your visit to London. Apart from this, it does not justify the price of £50 to stay in a very small bedroom where you can easily hear everyone walking and chatting every single time of day and night. The breakfast is OK but I doubt you will end up having a great rest.

title: Harry potter eat your heart out!
text: I travel to London on a regular basis in order to accompany an elderly relative. When I do this I spend a couple of nights in London to do some theatre so need to find convenient but affordable accommodation. I knew when I booked this hotel that I was in a single room with a shared bathroom which I did not mind as I only use the room to sleep, I did not however expect to be in a converted cleaning cupboard under the stairs without even a small wash basin. I knew that things were not going to be perfect when I arrived at the hotel (which I must admit was in a fairly good location) and went to check in. The receptionists (one French and one far eastern) both seemed as though English was far from their second language and seemed not to understand the simplest of questions. I eventually was given my key to room 107 and was told it was on the first floor. I went up in the lift as advised only to find that rooms 101 to 106 were signposted but no 107. I searched for several minutes but eventually went back to reception only to be told 'it is there somewhere'. After a second futile search I went back to reception and insisted that one of them show me where the room was! I then realised why they did not show me in the first place

title: Dårligt dårligt
text: Jeg var der og skulle bruge hotellet for fire nætter. På grund af deres dårligt hygiejne valgte at annullere min bookning. Fik ingen penge tilbage men fik en sur mail som jeg vedhæfter her. ((Good afternoon, Unfortunately to get your money back will not be possible, as my colleague explained to you previously that your booking was an advanced purchase booking in this case this is not refundable. if you wish please speak with booking.com If you have any further questions please do not hesitate to contact us. Thank you Kind regards, Nicki))

title: Good location - Lacking in Good old fashioned service
text: Called the Ibis a day or two prior to our arrival date tFo organize an early check-in availability of getting a better room as I had worked as Front Office Shift Leader at this hotel property many years ago when it was still the Ramada West London. As we were celebrating our 2nd honeymoon, I was very excited to show my husband where I used to live (around the corner in Redcliffe Gardens), play (at The Troubadour) and work! To sum up the experience - very poor communication especially with consierge and management. Lacking in warmth and hospitality. I get that it is a budget hotel and it is predominantly staffed by foreign workers but there are cheaper hotels out there that make you feel welcome and will go out of their way to ensure you have a good stay. If you want a quick basic, head down on pillow, in/out experience this is probably the place for you.

title: Tiny, smelly rooms with even smaller bathrooms - you can find a better hotel!
text: The room we had was very small - a full size bed barely fit and the bathroom...what a joke! Imagine an airplane bathroom with a tiny shower. They keep your key when you leave - not sure why they insisted on this, but they did! You stand in a line for a breakfast that consists of toast and cereal in the smallest dining room I've ever seen! It was also very loud! The location was ideal, but there are tons of other options on the same road!
