title: Not the Best
text: This was my fourth trip to London and this was definitely not the best room I've had, even at the same price level. I'm used to small rooms, but the bathroom was akin to a Port-a-Potty. Some of the bathrooms in the photos on this site are nice compared to what I had. My bedroom window was held shut with a piece of rope

title: Very disappointing
text: The hotel lobby was fabulous but misleading! To say my room was 'dated' would be an understatement, dingy, old and in need of TLC. I was here on business and definitely willl not be coming back.

title: Uninspiring and confused staff
text: Stayed here for a 5-days course. The room was tidy and dark, so course facilities were all in the basement with no windows, so it was 5 long days. The staff in the reception had the best intentions, but appeared rather inexperienced why the service level on some request lacked a bit. The hotel restaurant has a good deal for either steak or lobster, but also this place is poorly decorated, lacks atmosphere, and there are of course no windows. If the price happens to be really good, then it's okay, if not I would go elsewhere.

title: Cheap accommodation, but...
text: Six flights of narrow stairs to negotiate with bags, no lift. Unable to open and use the wardrobe without first sliding the bed to the far side of the room. No desk to work on. No iron or ironing board in room. Five day stay without a single service of the room/change of towels etc. Price was good but I wouldn't stay again.

title: Disappointing
text: On the plus side, the room (large studio?) was spotlessly clean

title: Not a four star hotel by any standards
text: Okay the location is fantastic, the service is fare, the concierge is very good. BUT. The rooms are very small, the breakfast is limited to same options everyday. The dining room is in the basement and is very small. Surprisingly, this hotel has an Indian theme, it should be an international Hilton. The art work is good, but I did not like the smoke sticks they light at the entrance every night, its smill is very strong. Also they put us in a room next to a small housekeeping storage room, every now and then there is someone talking or making noise in the room, I found it hard to take a nap during day time. The price is really too much for the hotel. You better off paying similar rates at better hotels in the same area. Also the room carpet was very dark and filthy. It is late 2013 and still there is no free Internet in the room, there is a sharge of £10 / 24 hours.

title: Great price in a pricey town!
text: Small room & bathroom. friendly knowledgable staff. Great location near "22 bus" & Victoria station. The beds were a bit springy, but you get what you pay for. Breakfast was fantastic!!!

title: OK for 1 night if you get it at a very discount price
text: Had a twin room, budget room decor, bigger bathroom in a touring caravan. Luggage store fantastic. Breakfast poor. Handy location. Pleased we didnt pay full price!

title: ...booking.com victim
text: ...so, some time you have a good hotel in a good place but when you book the room you realy don't know what's waiting for you. I was on the populars web site for find a hotel, and 9 time on 10 was perfect. But this time, i book a room...on the street! I can't immagine how a manager can rent a room at ONE METER to the street. No store, so i have a street light all the night, noise, funny for the game me and my stepson we play: try to reconnaise the language the people speak! The hotel was clean and good, but not all the room at the groundflor. Forget the room to 101 to 107, if you book a room, ask a first floor...

title: No recomendable
text: Small hotel, too small. Despite is clean. Bathrooms too small like a cabin of a vessel. Not room even in the shower. Too small rooms. If you travel in a couple and need a duble bed room, please don't accept room number 102. Is like cabin of "Marx" brother's film. Incredible. Continental breakfast is for only: toast, cheese orange juice, coffee or tea. That's all.

title: beware of Hanover Hotel
text: I made reservations at the hanover hotel, st. georges st. london for december 3-6, 2004 little did i know that this was a bank holiday, upon arriving there i was told i did not have a reservation even though i had a confirmation # and email in hand, this was because they did not want to honor my internet rate of 59 pounds per night and wanted a walk in rate of 89 per night. we went to the hotel down the street, new england hotel and were given a room and great service, it seems hanover hotel has a reputation for pretending not to speak english, and leaving people without a room, i hope this is passed on to travelers.

title: We wouldn't do this again
text: We were booked into this hotel for two separate one night stays in August 2008. The hotel was chosen primarily for its location in the Victoria area. When checking in for the first stay, we were immediately redirected to the Airways Hotel across the road. For the second stay, we were initially allocated a room at the Hanover. This room was on the lower ground floor (below street level), and was tiny. So tiny that it was impossible to use if you had luggage, as the double bed was the only place where luggage could be stored and opened. The bed itself looked to be well past its ‘due for replacement’ date. We asked if we could have a bigger room, and again found ourselves at the Airways. The Hanover generally has a run down appearance, and movement between floors is via narrow staircases. The staff are courteous while not particularly friendly, and helpful (room change request was handled well, and we were assisted with our luggage on the trip across the road). We’ve put a review of our stays in the Airways on Trip Advisor under that hotel.

title: Faulty Towers!
text: I`ll keep this brief. The floor in my room was on a slant so when i laid in the bed my feet were higher than my head. Thats actually quite funny but thats as good as it got! The bathroom door did not close or lock. The hot tap would not turn off. The balcony was used as an ashtray by prior guests and not cleaned up. The continental breakfast consisted of 2 slices of toast and a bowl of cereal. But for and additional charge of £3.50 you could upgrade to the English breakfast which was made up of 1 sausage 1 rasher of bacon 1 fried egg and half a dozen baked beans. The front door is supposed to be open 24hrs but on returning back late one night at the unsociable hour of 12.30 it was locked. I know its a budget accomodation but i expected more for £89 a night.

title: Average hotel, good location but room not great
text: Stayed at this hotel for one night recently for work. Pros - good location short walk from Victoria station, good price for London...43 pounds for one night in a triple room, place to leave luggage for free on leaving day, also were accommodating with early check in, bed comfortable, quiet area Cons - freezing shower you could not stay under the water! Needs a better clean...dusty behind TV, no view of out window just a wall

title: Broom Cupboard with a Bed
text: Visited for business, nice welcome but this is where the quality stopped. My appointed room was tiny in the basement. The bathroom was poor - no bigger than a wardrobe - toilet was positioned under the sink such that it was impossible to sit normally on it and the seat was stained with years of ingrained use. Shower door off its hinges. Next to a fire door to rear of hotel which guests/staff were using as some sort of smoking area til late at night with commensurate disturbance, further compounded by the constant drone from the hotels aircon units attached to the outside wall at the back of my room. Breakfast was adequate. Only saving grace was outstanding little Italian restaurant up the road called o sole mio!

title: Look at the pictures I posted. A picture is worth 1000 words.
text: Cons. Old. Run down. Not worth what you pay for. No safety deposit box. Although it states that one exists on the website Pros. Location is fantastic. They’ll probably tell you what they told me. That they have newly renovated rooms, and that is what you see on their website. Just none available at the time. I was there for 5 night and asked to move to one of the renovated rooms when they became available. They claim that all the renovated rooms were fully booked.. I don’t think they exist.

title: Not again in this lifetime!
text: First of all the address is misleading. The Hotel is NOT on Gloucester Terrace. It is on Craven. We walked from Paddington Station with our bags and couldn't find the hotel until we asked a taxi driver. Whlie the lobby is very nice (and air conditioned) the room was VERY small, VERY hot, and VERY much not worth the money. It was the most expensive room in which I stayed over my week's visit to Great Britain and was least worth the money. Although we had intended to pay cash everywhere we stayed (and did everywhere else), the Brunel took the liberty of charging the credit card with which I had secured the reservation via an online booking service for the first night of our stay before I arrived. WiFi was 5 pounds per day. Use of a computer was 2 pounds per half hour. There were 4 (sometimes 5) channels from which to choose on the small, outdated television set. The best thing about the staff was that they ignored you unless questioned directly

title: Shakespeare
text: Not a bad hotel, but the single star rating is because there was no hot water for a shower. Out of three nights there, there was only heated water on one occasion! Pretty poor for a London Hotel. Nice waffles though!

title: Awesome location, but very old and outdated
text: First of all, the location is really good. It's next to a underground station and in the center of London. Unfortunately, it's really old and too small. I was with my school class for 1 week in London, we had to sleep in the "basement". It was hard to sleep, because the underground was really loud. The service is friendly and helpful, but the hotel and the furniture are just too old. Pro -> Location,Service Contra -> Sleep Quality, Rooms, Cleanliness

title: Dissapointing
text: The hotel is in a good location on a quiet street in Earls Court near the tube station and many options for meals. Half of the staff is very friendly (Mohamed at the front desk in particular was extremely helpful), and half I would say grumpy, especially the guy who was at the desk Sunday morning before 7 AM. There is no air conditioning so you need to leave your windows open but there are no window screens. The bathrooms are really small, about the same as a cruise ship. There is one small elevator that seemed to be enough. Breakfast was about what I expected for continental, but it never changed. The breakfast attendants were very efficient and after breakfast they doubled as room attendants. The rooms offer no dresser or chest of drawers to unpack in so you are basically working out of your suitcase.

title: Not what we were hoping for
text: The reason I booked this hotel was its fantastic website promising ' a new concept in hotels...to offer you some of the best London hotel accommodation, with excellent service and facilities, all at a value price.' As a young couple this really sounded up our street! I kept an eye on the price of a Grovsner Room as it fluctuated right up to £165 per night and after finding it for just under £80 I jumped at the chance of a 'great deal' expecting a fresh, vibrant and funky hotel with comfortable, contempory rooms (again a reflection of the website). On arriving at the hotel we werre definatley impressed with the location and the hotel building (it really was a Notting Hill setting). The staff were helpful as promised and everything was looking good! The only problem was on enterering our room... The furniture looked like something you would pick up at a car boot sale and the bathroom was so small it couldn't even fit a sink in it which subseqently was in our bedroom. It definatley was not the type of room we had been promised...and paid extra for as a Grovsner Room. I even had to call downstairs to double check we had the right room. I know that finding a room in London for under £100 a night can be a challenge but I really believe that Umi Hotels are promoting a false idea of what the hotel has to offer.

title: budget option with low standars
text: we stayed for 5 days and the rooms were not very clean and they did not provide you many facilities. For examble they didn't have brush and hangers for towels in the toilets .Also room had in some places dust. But the breakfast was nice.

title: Mr
text: My son and I stayed there for 4 days. By far the smallest room ever. Comfortable linen, Wi-Fi non existent, very noisy due to very thin walls! The location is good, next to Earls Court station. The cleaning and kitchen staff was very efficient and friendly. The breakfast is a typical low budget continental but this is expected.

title: Over priced tiny double room with bad quality
text: Me and my wife stayed at this hotel for 4 nights during a conference at Imperial College London. Pros + Good Location + Breakfast Quality (not the quantity) + Free wifi with good speed. Cons - Too Little space in the room and in the toilet - Asked for a kingsize double, but didn't even got a full double bed. It's kind of or bit bigger than semi double. - Not cheap compare to the facilities. - Hand written Invoice. - Quantity of the Breakfast: It's not buffet, it's served by the staffs. - Old fashioned furniture and window - Not Soundproof. You can hear the sound/talk from the other rooms. Overall Not recommended.

title: Atrocious customer service
text: Hotel made an error in booking dates for my business stay and then insisted this was non-refundable and non-transferrable. Initially they accepted that the error was theirs but then when trying to change the booking changed their mind about accepting any financial responsibility and rather than transferring the payment were insisting on full payment for the new booking (which if course is fine) and no refund for the erroneous booking!

title: Tiny tiny at a steep price
text: Positive: nice staff, lift,clean 24 hrs reception.nice bathroom.our room (205) was bright and overlooking the road. Negative: double bed was placed in tha corner of 8 sqm room. One the left side along the wall nowhere to step- on the right side there were exactly 12 cm to place a foot. Hard and short bed. Not a room to stay in though you could ( luckily we had others things to do)- lay in the bed with your feet on the outside and stare at a midget-tv fixed 2 m up on the wall. We had to have the window wide open to have two people sleeping with sufficient oxygen. The breakfast room was overcrowded and people who came late had to wait. We paid about 150 pounds for something which was worth half of that.

title: Dirty!
text: The location of this hotel is really good, as it is close to the tube stations, Oxford Street, Covent Garden etc. We felt lucky at the beginning, but when we checked in to our rooms we saw that the sheets were dirty (there were short male hairs on the pillow), and the bin wasn't emptied. We told this to the receptionist in the evening (expecting that he would give us clean sheets), he only said that he would get the room cleaned the next day. However, the next day, after coming back, we saw that the bin was emptied, but the pillow cases were still the same! The breakfast and the location are good, but I won't be staying here again.

title: Good value, but i was charged twice
text: Excellent value rooms, with a generous breakfast. Location is perfect for central London. However, i was double charged for one night of my stay. Be very careful when checking in or out, to make sure the details for your stay are correct. Also, when you return home, check that no overcharging has taken place. I really liked this accommodation, but after 3 weeks back home, am still waiting for my refund - be warned!

title: Awful service
text: The location is nice but that is about all that the hotel has to offer. The breakfast that is included consists of small boxes of cereal milk and coffee. While we were there we had to place a call to the airport. At the lobby we were greeted by a young man who said thwy did not extend that courtesy to their guests to go use a payphone. The iron they loaned us did not work. We have stayed in london before and loved it. Definitely would never stay here again and DO NOT RECOMMEND!

title: OK, but would not stay there again
text: I stayed at this hotel in September of 2004. I decided to write this review because I wanted to let the people know that since September of 2004, the ownership of this hotel changed, and definitely not for the better. I agree with previous travelers that the location of this hotel is perfect, however, for this kind of value you can find something better in London. The rooms were very tiny and the new staff was not friendly at all. So if you read previous "perfect" reviews, keep in mind that things changed, and you might not find the hotel you were hoping for. Be careful.

title: I would not recommend
text: No air conditioning. Our room was small and we had to carry all of our luggage up four flights of stairs. The breakfast however was good and good service for breakfast. There was a step up to the bathroom that was NOT fun to negotiate in the middle of the night. Also, our shower drain took about 20 minutes to drain. The area the hotel is in in great though.

title: can't sleep well cos bed & noisy environment
text: I stayed there for 4 nights, location is good, but room is so small and not clean. don't like it. it is not value for money.

title: Clean, good showers but very noisy and couldn't have my breakfast.
text: Single room too hot and extremely noisy from the lorries that start going by at 5am. Paid extra for breakfast but after waiting 15mins at reception to find out where to go, there were no staff about and so had to leave. On a positive note, rooms very clean and showers hot and powerful.

title: Smallest room I've ever seen
text: Excellent location and clean enough but rooms extremely small and size of beds in a doubleroom way too small for two adults!!!

title: Hotel with rooms smaller than 8m2
text: Probably the smallest room in the world for 85£/night !!! without breakfast. True, we are in Marble Arch area, but not in the chique part of it though. True, it is 5 min walk from the famous Primark megastore, but that is the only positive note, together with a friendly reception. For the remainder, if you like to sleep in a 8m2 double bedroom WITHOUT toilet nor shower (and like to go upstairs therefore), then this is your pick. For us, never again.

title: Don't
text: Central location is wonderful. All else is third world.

title: Stay in Marble Arch Inn
text: Location is very good. But: 1) Room is extremely SMALL and overpriced. 2) Hotel in website mentioned that BB basis, but when you check-in the say that it is only "Bed Basis". 3) I never seen such “small shower”, you hardly move in it, really. 4) Phone in the room doesn’t work if you would like to reach receptionist or in an emergency case. 5) There is almost no space in the room to move. 6) Seems that owner split 1 rooms into 3-4 rooms and re-designed in order to make a revenue. 7) No elevators and so small stairs, you need to carry luggage by yourselves. 8) From room you can hear what is happening in all other rooms and room above. 9) Staff grooming - No Grooming at all 10) Check out time at 11:00am and they start to call you an hour in advance for check out I would never recommend this hotel to anyone!!!

title: Disappointing
text: Initial impressions were good - excellent location with helpful and efficient staff on the front desk. The room , however , was a let down - dark , with a small double bed and cramped bathroom ( although the shower and toiletries were good ). Perhaps I was unlucky , but the lower ground floor facing onto the street was particularly noisy both from passers by and heavy vehicles whose engines running as they waited in the street set things vibrating in the room. Breakfast was included in my rate , but small plates for the buffet ( too small for toast , scrambled egg and a hash brown ) and a single cup of coffee seemed mean with much better value available nearby.

title: I wouldn't recommend
text: <in my previousl 4 tripadvisor hotel reviews, I gave 3 times 5 stars and 1 time 4 stars> My wife and I stayed in the Holiday Inn Regent Park hotel between the 4-8/6/2008. We have encountered numerous times when we were told false information by the staff: 1. we asked for a double bed room via email and got confirmation. When we got there, no double bed room was available. 2. The receptionist (named Jude) told us that this is only temporary and someone will move our belonging to another room with double bed, the next morning, while we are out travelling. This was not done. 3. We asked for a wakeup call at 7:30 and received it 20 minutes later. We complain and were told that the wake up list says 7:50. 4. the concierge told us that all events start at 11:00 on Sundays, which is simply not true. On the other side, John, the receptionist was really nice, professional and helpful. I'm describing this as this seems like a pattern, and not a random mistake. We saw another complain earlier in the reviews and wondered about the odds that this will happen to us. Well...it just did. Besides that the hotel location is great. Only 100m from the tube, tesco and pret a manger. In addition, if you go to this hotel, 50m north to the hotel, there is a construction site. We haven't stayed in a north room, so we're not sure about the noise coming from this site, but this should also take under consideration. In addition, the hotel is very clean (so say my wife) and provide all the needed facilities - safe in the room, minibar (cost money), TV (not LCD), playstation (cost money), ok bed and shower. All in all, I wouldn't recommend going to this hotel, just because the problems we had with 3 out of 4 staff members.

title: Curious loos
text: WARNING - not for the squeamish. With a rack rate for the room of £450 one would at least expect some nicely fluffy loo paper rather than paper which is more like the infamous Izal ("Rough or smooth side for you?") which we used for tracing at primary school. Getting to it was an interesting experience. The two holders are placed below the seat level and under a shelf. In order to reach the paper, this makes it necessary to almost put your head down the loo, a none too pleasant experience. The suggestions for the hotel is to reposition at least one of the holders up the wall, perhaps to beside the redundant phone socket. The suggestion for yourself is to remove the roll of paper from its holder before you sit down. Good luck! The bed is decidedly firm. Remembering the high rack rate for a basic room (B&B = £450), I was surprised to discover that there is no free Wi-Fi and that the rates for going onto the internet while in the hotel are extremely high.

title: We came from the deserts of Namibia to a London Hotel with No Water
text: The location and the staff were friendly. But the water to our room was cut off and whilst we were told it was getting fixed we left at 11am the next day without having been able to have a shower or flush the toilet. It would have been nice if they could have made a plan as it was our last night in the UK from Namibia and the price was very high for us. Even in Namibia our hotels have water.

title: Not quite as it seems
text: Don't look at the photographs and believe your room will look like that. Location good as 5 mins away from Old Street underground station. On entering there is a sewer manhole beneath the entrance mat and boy can you smell that it is there. The reception staff are quite abrupt, they will ask to photocopy your id and credit card, don't let them as this is stored together then you are open to someone using your card no as they will also have your address! I was offered an upgrade for a cash supplement which I took them up on as the small room is really small, I waited in reception for a receipt as I believe they don't normally give one from reading other reviews. The apartment was ok, comfortable bed, adequate kitchen with a fridge with ice compartment, microwave, washing machine, kettle and toaster, tea, coffee and milk was also supplied. Shower needs a bit of a clean but overall the apartment was clean. Television with freesat though not all channels were available. I was in the room (8b) above the main entrance so it was really noisy with the door slamming every time anyone came in or left which was in the early hours of the morning. There's a great little indian café next door that does some great food you can take back to your room, rice and 2 currys only £3 but tasted really good, I couldn't eat it all! I won't be returning to this apartment.

title: Nice except the noise isolation
text: Impossible to sleep I could hear the neighboµr the next rented flat like if they were in the same room. And the toilet were very noisy the pump. nice decoration but if it is impossible to sleep it doesnt worth it!!

title: The luxury of Kitch
text: The entrance was obscure and a friend visiting tthought I was staying in a brothel ..lHe smell in the entrance was parculiar. In any case they tried to give the appartment a luxurious feeling but with a taky taste and hence the pictures look great but when you get there you do not feel comfortable. The reception service you felt similar to the way they treat people at NY Kennedy airport ,, not precisely welcoming . the apartment room was OK and I did like the fact of having space., although having said that the entire interior spacing was bizar and nothing worked. out, the bathroom was probably 1square meter and the floo r heat ing was so hot that tit resembled a sauna + on bare feet was impossible to stand on the foloor

title: An odd little place
text: ***Note: This place also goes by the name of Langham Apartments. The Rivington name may have been created because of the many negative reviews for Langham Apartments.*** First some advice: If you are a tourist visiting London, this is not the place for you. Old Street is a down at the heels neighborhood in east London and it is far from most typical tourist attractions. If you are doing business in the City of London, however, this place is both convenient and inexpensive. You'd do well to check in on the early side (and call in advance to ensure that there will be someone there to greet you because the reception is not always staffed). The building itself is a bit of a rabbit warren that is under construction...a bit of dust present, though my room was spotless. I stayed in the "studio flat". The flat is furnished to a pretty high standard, with top quality bathroom fixtures and lots of marble/granite on the walls and floor. The bed was extremely comfortable. The room is exceptionally tiny, however and suitable for no more than one person. The bathroom is practically non-existent...the toilet takes up all the floor space, and the sink is too small to shave in. You'll want to shower, shave and dry off inside the (very nicely appointed by the way) shower stall. My first floor (second floor for Americans) flat was very noisy: Street noise was noticable throughout the night and starting around 11pm a disco beat started...sounds like there was a nearby disco, or even one in the basement. The disco continued till two or three AM. So in summary, OK for a single person for one night if you are doing business nearby and can sleep through ambient noise. Completely unsuitable for tourists and light sleepers.

title: Needs Renovations
text: I stayed in the Marlyn Lodge unit 210 for a week with my wife. Unit 210 was a 1 bedroom unit that's needs to be renovated. The bathroom was old and the tub was peeling with rust. The kitchen was adequate but had no dishwasher and had older appliances. We did not use the washing machine so we do not know how that work but there is also no dryer. We arrived on a Saturday when there is no one to leave bags with if arriving before 2pm. We were told to leave bags in Liverpool Street train station which is 1 mile away if we got there early. I am not sure if all the units are in the same condition but this unit needs to be updated. The good things about the Marlyn Lodge are the wifi and good location with access to underground, trains and grocery stores. I would not stay here again

title: Mixed feelings
text: The location is superb & the staff are extremely friendly & helpful. However, I feel the staff are let down by the fact that this hotel is in serious need of a make-over & does not deserve the 4 star rating it claims to have. If you plan on staying at this hotel I would skip breakfast as it was well below par & seriously overpriced. There are plenty of nice eateries in the local so you won

title: Dirty
text: I arrived late the first night to find that my bed sheets were full of somebody's hair. They apologised and gave me another room with clean sheets. You'd think that after this they would do anything to make the rest of your permanence enjoyable. The second night again I walked in at 6pm and found that the sheets and towels had not been changed and the room had not been cleaned.

title: Awful stay....NEVER AGAIN!
text: We stayed in this hotel on the 13th and 14th June as we were going to ministry of sound on the 13th and wanted to stay close! We booked a deluxe double room at £100 a night. We got in to our room (number 322) the room was dark and boiling hot. We noticed the air conditioning unit was switched off at the wall so we switched it on for it to blow out hot air...not helpful at all. We opened the windows to let some air in to find a train track right next to our room with trains going past every 10-20 minutes. The floor in the bathroom was dirty, luckily we had some wipes with us so we were able to wipe over the floor. The shower took about 10 minutes to reach a warm temperature and when it was a suitable temperature it would fluctuate from boiling to freezing. We ate in the restaurant for quickness on the Friday and found that the meat was very chewy, service was slow and then they wacked on a 10% service charge, the waitress actually didn't add this charge on when using the card machine, however she soon realised and made us pay it even though we didn't feel they warranted a tip. Our room was also above the restaurant which plays extremely loud music from 8-11 it was getting so loud that we couldn't even hear the tv! When we asked when it was going to be stopping we also informed them about the air conditioning in our room, it was working but they just "forgot" to give us the remote. It seems our money goes on the owner branding the curtains and bedding with the hotel name...they even had their toiletries named after the hotel of which was actually spelt incorrectly...gives you ok hope when they can't get the spelling of their own hotel correct on all of their branded items! I will say that the room and en suite were of a good size and the bed was relatively comfy however these are the only positive comments i have about the hotel. I would never stay there again and would never recommend the hotel to anyone!!

title: Not the best for the price
text: Upon arriving I checked in at the office, as others have said I wasn't thrilled about the copy of my passport. In addition to this I was asked for £250 in cash to pay for my room. When I asked to pay by card as I was travelling for business, the gentleman on reception pulled a face. I asked if they had a machine and he said yes but that there would be a 5% charge for the priviledge, he showed me some small print but this was not on my online booking. Tired, I agreed to pay, he then asked for a £250 pre authorisation which was fine but I didn't understand why they then needed written details of my credit card. My room was on the floor level with the road which was by and large fine noise wise apart from when someone used the front door I could hear every footstep, breath, conversation etc. The room was clean but worn, you can definitely get better for £125 per night. It put me in mind of a student bedsit, none of the furniture or soft furnishings matches. The shower room was tiny but adequate, towels are very small though! There was a wardrobe, plenty ofplugs, iron, kitchen, tv, DVD and phone. All fine and in working order. Bed was fairly comfy but no duvet just a sheet and a blanket. The best thing going for this 'hotel' is it's location. A five minute walk to Paddington at most, loads of nice restaurants and bars. Overall I wouldn't recommend it though, it's not an apartment, the staff are quite cold and rooms are worn.

title: Ruined our weekend away
text: We checked in knowing that the pictures of the apartment's were to an acceptable standard. First of all, I like friendly smiling people at the reception, and if I give that I expect to have it back in return.

title: Very basic
text: Good location...but very very basic, could really do with a Complete renovation. If you just want some where to lay your head for the night...and not fussed about a very basic hotel it would be ok, its also very hot and noisy.

title: London in another way!
text: The hotel location is super! The hotel staff ia very nice and helpful. There is a luggage room for free! There is the USB charger for mobile phones in the room and you don't Need the adaptor. Breakfast is 3.50 pounds and you can choose bread, jam, butter, coffee, juice, tra, yougurt. Nothing really special, but the price is low, so it's ok. There is the bathroom in the room, very small and an hairdryer. The price ia too expensive for the hotel rooms. Very very small and not so comfortable for the price you pay. On the other hand, the hotel is 5 minutes walking from King's Cross station, so Easy to go everywhere. A special Word for the staff at the reception, very kind very helpful, very nice!!!

title: Grubby hotel and poor facilities
text: We needed somewhere local to Kings Cross station so I chose this hotel as it was a good location. However, the room was tiny, there was no shelf space for storing bathroom essentials so everything had to go in the wardrobe. I tried to refill a kettle but the sink wasn't big enough to fit the kettle so I thought I would refill a bottle of water. That wouldn't fit either. I had to use a small glass to do the job. There was a coating of dust on the 'refreshment' tray. Overall not the best experience.

title: Hold the Mold!
text: We loved the location of The Grange Lodge B and B. It's a lovely quiet area, it felt very much at home. The ladies that we saw running the hotel, were friendly and knowledgeable. The room was small but perfectly adequate to sleep in. We stayed in one of the only rooms with an ensuite. The ensuite had a mold issue and by the time we left, I was sick. For the price of the nightly stay, it was mostly worth it--the ceiling needed a good washing and the peeling drywall with the mold behind should be removed.

title: compact
text: when we arrived told not to use bannister as painted not much use if you needed help to get upstairs, room small bathroom really small had to stand in shower to shave would be impossible wash face in sink due to its size bedroom not very clean and bed hard against wall, kettle was sited on peddle bin, had to leave building at rear for breakfast to conservatory in yard, location good for shepards bush green empire but would not stay more than one night here

title: Well What Can I Say
text: On arriving at the Grantley, we were showed to our room. It was very small and bathroom even smaller. The toilet being practically on top of the sink, no room to move. The shower was so slow wondered if it was ever going to work. The bed was lumpy and flat pillows with no extra ones if needed. The room was on the main road hence very noisy and single glazed windows, so no sleep the first night. The wall between rooms was so thin that every noise could be heard from the adjoining bathroom and I don't mean the pulling of the flush. On mentioning these things in the morning we were asked what did we want them to do about it (not what I call customer friendly). Yes it is close to the tube station but that is about all that can be said for it. The price you pay is not the quality you get. Somebody needs to take a long hard look at this hotel. At the end of the day not a pleasant experience.

title: Great location but very basic facilities
text: I stayed with a friend at 1 Lesham Gardens for four nights. The hotel has a great location

title: Sorley Disappointing
text: On arrival from the outside it looked like it needed a good lick of paint. inside and the reception area was well kept and made you think your first thought outside was a little harsh so you give the benefit of the doubt. Then you find your way to your room you open the door expecting a boutique room but no! miss matched furniture.. holes in the wall filled then not repainted.. the window blind broken unable to open and no curtains to keep the light out so you don't get much sleep but with the beds and the waifer thin pillows that have seen better days. after a full day of wondering around the sights of London you want to have a nice refreshing shower but then the shower!! the shower head alone must have years of god knows what on the head of it but you have no other option but use it... the bathroom it's self is beyond small.. the fixtures and fittings have seen better days.. If I could offer abit of advice is that 1 Lexham Gardens is in need of a complete refit or even some money spending on it RC

title: Very budget
text: The room was in the basement, through a maze of doors. It was the smallest little room and the bathroom was only for skinny people as it was the size of a matchbox. This room or accommodation would be fine for a single traveller, however my partner and I found it too small for over three days and checked into another hotel. If you're after budget not frills accommodation for one, is a Stella location of London this place ticks the boxes. It was clean and well serviced and staff were friendly. Breakfast was just plain and simple with again no frills.

title: Expensive for a lousy hotel
text: The hotel is in a generally beautiful neighborhood. The exterior is beautiful, as well as the lobby. Once you step out of the lobby and into the hall to catch the elevator, your dreams are shattered. Tiny, dated elevator that barely fits 2 people with luggage. Everything is very dated, the walls need new paint. Rooms are dingy. You only get one sheet on the bed, no comforter or duvet. There is no air conditioning in the rooms, you have to rely on a 12 inch fan and an open window. The rooms are also very small. I would never stay here again, nor recommend for anyone to stay. If their prices were lower, it would justify the condition of their rooms.

title: Be aware of cancellation polcy
text: Please be very aware of the canceelation policy as i just lost out of 400 euro after cancelling the booking!!!

title: Not as good as you expect from this brand
text: Perfectly happy with the staff I met but surprised that there is no restaurant for evening meals - only a few local takeway menus. Given how little there is in the neighbourhood you'd have thought they would do good trade every day. More importantly though, I was amazed to see that the only hot breakfast items on both days I stayed there were sausages (thousands of them!!) and scrambled eggs. Have bacon, tomatoes, baked beans and the like not made it as far as Limehouse yet? The mattress was poor - you could feel the individual springs clearly, as though the stuffing had been removed. One finaly gripe, the bin in my room hadn't been emptied after the previous guest had left. Were I that way inclined, I could have had a good root through the paperwork they had thrown away!

title: Surround sound
text: The hotel is located on Old Street, a very busy road. No matter where your room is you hear the noise from the road. Walls are paper thin so you hear your neighbours very clearly. Writing this right now at 1 am listening to rowdy neighbours next door. The hotel has been converted from typically badly built london office block, never designed for hospitality so you get to hear people above stomping around. If a good night sleep is low on your list of prioroties while in london then this is the hotel for you! Stayed at the earls court easyhotel and that was much quieter. On a more positive note the rooms are a decent size at barbican.

title: For one night and one night only....
text: when it says you pay for what you get, I could have been in a nicer hotel, with better facilities and a cooked breakfast for a tiny bit more. Room with windows is in fact windows that are obscured and cannot be opened.

title: You get what you pay for
text: The staff on reception were extremely helpful and friendly. The apartment was a fair size and had the basic amenities included (microwave etc.). Location was perfect for Hyde Park and Paddington Station. The flight of stairs was long, with no elevator/lift facility. There were a few cracks in the walls and windows on the stairways too. Our apartment had a strange smell coming from the sink whenever it was turned on too.

title: Awful
text: We were moved to this hotel because we couldn't stay at it's sister property (so paddington) for which we had originally booked. I'm not sure how much a room at this place should be, but we paid the £90 a night for so paddington, there was no breakfast (we were told that we could eat at the other property (5 minute walk away)) the room was tiny and not the cleanest, and very noisy. I know London is a busy place but it sounded like we were sleeping at piccadilly circus. On the plus side the shower was good, however there was no maid service so the bed was never made and the towels not changed. Do not stay here even if it's for £25 a night.

title: I wouldn't recommend
text: The website and the photos make this hostel looks like a good place to stay but it's not a place I would stay again. I booked a private room with a private shower for my brother and I. The room was as expected since it is a hostel however, there was NO towels, wash cloth or bath soap, just room amenities. I went down to the service desk to inquire about the towels and the front desk guy said I've to pay for it. I would've been okay if that was communicated upon check-in or stated on the site but there are not. Room for improvement: They do need to work on their guest service skills and experience so the guest can feel welcome and home away from away. Inform the guests of any information needed so there's not element of surprise.

title: Average
text: Staff was great and breakfast was fairly good. However, this was the smallest room I have been in. I stayed with a friend in a twin room. It consisted of a bunk bed and just the place to put our luggage: there was no wardrobe nor table where to put our things. Whenever we wanted to go out of the room, we had to move our luggage in order to open the door.

title: Not so good
text: The hostel is well located, a couple of tube stations away from Westminster. There is also the bus option on the stop right in front of the hostel. Shower is very small. There is no power socket near the beds. The staff is friendly and very helpful when it comes to buying tickets to attractions.

title: OK for a night
text: Shared a quad room with sink and shower. Nice looking reception and dining area. Beds were comfortable, but the room was a little dusty and could have been cleaner. Staff didn't seem very helpful. Wouldn't stay again.

title: Sad disapointment
text: I stayed recently in what I thought was a REALLY nice room.. service was excelent.. UNTIL it was time to sleep. There is a partially frosted glass wall which connects the bathroom to the rest of the room and is right next to the bed. It is simply not enough to protect from light pouring out of the bathroom and straight on the bed.. which wakes up the occupant every time the light is turned on.

title: Small odd shaped room in poor decorative order
text: Stayed for four nights and would not recommend it. The room was hideous but the kitchen area, up a few stairs was new. Three random plates and a few mismatched glasses. Bathroom small but adequate. Small double bed with cheap bedding and extremely soft mattress. Net curtains with view of walls covered In very noisy aircon units and extractor fans so a constant humming in the room. No bedside lights, told this would be fixed ~ next week~. 30 p!us spotlights in ceiling and had to get out of bed to turn lights off! Walls in sleeping area tiled and artexed, a bit disconcerting. Right in the heart of shoreditch so really good location .

title: Too expensive and uncomfortable
text: We have stayed at this hotel, the room was soo small and the breakfast was just few things without a restaurant they were leaving the tray in front of the door. the hotel is good for one night stand but for family and long stay I wouldnt recommend. the price is so high for this service.

title: Grotty and in need of a duster!!!!
text: We stayed here for one night! The room we were given was on the top floor which was like climbing a mountain the stairs are so steep and the staircase was covered in dust, so they changed our room straight way it was room 5 this was right next door to the reception this was a tiny cupboard with a computer and a booking book, the lobby ( this is the hallway into the hotel and rooms ) was tiny and diry. The room was falling to bits ply wood furniture that looked like it could fall down. Mould on the shower curtain, stains on the duvet cover dust everywhere and the windows do not shut. Then the breakfast that you get at 8 am regardless weather you want it at that time, this includes muffins, aqua water, and a pastry, some crackers. Please be warned do not stay here if it can be avoided !! Oh yes and the tube runs directly under the hotel and rock the floors.

title: The lovely disgusting place
text: Tony's a lovely magic place, we booked 2 rooms and we had a great time! Top moments were the following ones! "Hello Mr Tony, where's placed our room? - It's the one close to my counter, it's door to door, you will have the best wifi coverage inside the hostel! (he really was our neightbour, he slept on the floor indeed) "Excuseme mr Tony, there's no hot water (we awake him at two o'clock in the morning) - Then there's no hot water "But Mr.Tony, we need to have a shower! - It's ok, try using the cold water tap instead of the hot one (it seemed to be some kind of scramble for newcomers) What kind of breakfast will we have mr Tony? Surprise, it's a nice continental breakfast! (actually, next morning we found a stray on the floor and some dort stole the few things that were slighly eatable) We strongly recommend Tony's to the ones who loves the Phantom Manor or want to have a great time!

title: Disappointment
text: We were staying at room for five persons which is too small for that many people,also a bathroom was a size of the small closet, and the room was not very clean also the sheets on the bed seem not very well washed.Also we have waited more than its needed for the owner to give us a room key. On the other hand, positive thing was a good breakfast and kind staff.

title: Horrible
text: When we first got there the guy who worked in the reception wouldn't open the door for us even though he had monitors in his office showing him a family standing outside with their suitcases. The time was 6pm. We were five and got the smallest room possible. It was so small that we couldn't even place our suitcases anywhere. We had to take turns opening the suitcases and then place them on top of each other. It was not clean at all and there was dust all over the floor. When we got back to the hotel at night the room was literally like a sauna. It was nice of them to heat the rooms but not necessary at all. We asked for an extra towel to dry our hands with -didn't get one. The pillows were so hard that I had to sleep on my fluffy sweater. You can hear the vibrations of the tube so loud that it woke us up at 6am. The breakfast was served in plastic bags and were too sweet. The only good thing was the location and the staff. It was close to the Paddington Station, bus stations and restaurants. The guy who worked there was very polite and helpful. Wouldn't recommend this hotel if you're staying more than one night and with larger groups. There were a lot of things that happened that I just don't even have the time to write.

title: The cold shoulder..............
text: I booked this hotel via Hotwire and got a great price, i think it was circa £80 for the night. From a location point of view its not great. Its on the wrong side of the river for most tourist's. the nearest tube station is Vauxhall but i wouldn't want to make that walk too late at night or allow my wife to walk it late on her own. The hotel is very stylish with a great bar and the rooms are well appointed albeit slightly too close to the main railway line to Waterloo, but not too much noise. I had a major issue with my rooms air-conditioing in that it remained on all night at its lowest temperature, my stay was in December and it would have been warmer outside. I had to sleep with my head under the duvet, the shower was bliss but i hurriedly got dressed. My feet were still numb with cold as a stood at reception and asked, well demanded that they visit the room to validate my story......they didn't. If i was at a premier inn i would have received a refund, all i got was the offer of an coffee! I was told that the next time i booked i would be well looked after, had the email of the duty manager and we kept in touch. I emailed to book another room and bearing in mind i paid £80 last time.......£256!!!!! In summary not a great location, a good hotel with 1970's style customer service. If you get it at a great price go for it, if not then keep on looking.

title: Dont do it!
text: The only good thing here is the location. The reception staff are doing a favor that they are answering your questions. NO WIFI in the rooms and they are not doing anything to solve it. NOT RECOMMENDED!

title: Don't bother
text: I stayed here for one night. I chose it as it was close to Euston for an early train the following morning. The double room consisted of two single beds pushed together. Fine, but one was higher up than the other! The sheets didn't exactly smell fresh. The bedside light didn't work. Lighted flooded in from the hallway into the room. Unsurprisingly I didn't have a very good night's sleep! All this for a bargain £135 a night. My email of complaint was duly ignored. Never stay here.

title: Baaaaaaaaaaaaaad experience
text: Chunky old metal bar beds and too small. No closet hangers in the wardrobe????????????!!!!!!! No electric point near the mirror (shaving). Plastic curtains.... what the.... Breakfast is limited (to 6 pieces) 'Can I have some bacon please?' Yes, ONE piece. Friendly staff though - I feel for them to have to work there.

title: pretty awful
text: I wouldn't go as far as some people in dissing this place. It's a cheap, not-particularly-well-run place in a not-so-nice part of town, but it's not that bad! the people were quite nice and the beer was cold. I won't be back though!

title: Not great!
text: Really friendly people and decent shower room but shower was either hot or, hot and wi fi in room didn't work. Room was decent size and relatively clean if you didn't look too closely. Bedding clean but stained as were pillows. It's a cheap place to stay at close to amenities but not a nice area to stay in, noise was no problem though. A definite no for romance! Shared kitchen etc. nice. Wouldn't want to stay again.

title: Humidity and heating
text: The heating does not work and the room smells humidity so be careful and you have to pay for the wifi... the breakfast was good and the location too but , some rooms are not so confortable but the staff tried to hepl us .

title: Informed at 11am on day of check in that apartment uninhabitable with no satisfactory resolution. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND!
text: My stay "... was less than perfect..."! I didn't get to stay due to a 'supposed' PROBLEM with the toilet that UNBELIEVABLY couldn't be fixed by an emergency plumber, PLEASE, NO PERSON IN THEIR RIGHT MIND WOULD BELIEVE THIS STORY! We were only informed of the problem at 11.05am while on route to the apartment. The stress caused to me and my family was huge and the resolution of moving us to the ME hotel was less than satisfactory. It meant we were in the correct location (not impressed with an offer of an apartment at Hyde Park or near the Monument) but the move to a one bedroomed hotel room with a put me up bed in the living space and sharing one bathroom and toilet was not what I wanted from accommodation. This was not what I wanted as I was staying with my partner and her mother was to have her own room in the apartment. So, no I won't be recommending you to anyone nor will I be staying with you again. My guess is they had a better booking for more than one night and they just made this up to get rid of me. (supposed to be staying 3rd June for one night)

title: Slow service. Don't come if you want an efficient experience.
text: It took them over half an hour to serve our meals... when we folled up they just kept saying it was on thr way. People that arrived after us were served and finished their meals before ours were even served. When they arrived, they were luke warm and the rib eyes were hard as leather. Don't come here if you want a good pub experience.

title: Far, far away from luxory!
text: We were transferred from So sienna, in which we booked the room for our 5 night stay. SO Sienna had problem with water (which apperes to be common according to the staff). The So Quartier apartment was small, oldish and worn with many problems. For example the bathroom smelled mould (had to use my asthma pipe), the bathroom lock got stucked all the time and the tap in the "kitchen" was leaking. There were not enough dishes for four people. The windows were blurred (which made the apartment dark), but when I opened the window, I could see the reason why. Luckily we did not spend much time in this appartment! Pros: the stuff was friendly and close to underground and overground stations. Nice restaurant (Raw Brick) nearby with good pizza and pasta!

title: No one was at the front desk! No service, surprisingly bad service apartment. 最悪のサービスと呑気なカスタマーサポート。
text: Go Nativeのチェーン。立地は良いが、オフィス街なので日曜日夜は周辺のレストランも店も開いていないので要注意。 １ベッドルームの部屋は、こじんまりとしているが快適。キッチンには食器や紅茶も揃っており調理はしやすい。洗濯乾燥機も便利。シーツは変えてくれないし、清掃も無し。自分でゴミ出しの必要もある。 問題は基本的な対応。午後８時半までしかフロントに人がいないということで、７時半に到着。 数人のゲストがフロントの前にたむろしていたが、従業員の姿は皆無。そのうち皆さん諦めて誰もいなくなった。が、さて困った。カスタマーサポートに電話してみたら、部屋のカギを用意してあるはずだから事務所に入って金庫を開けろという。フロントの人間は不在だが飲みかけのコーヒーに、点けっぱなしのラジオがデスクの上に放置。嫌な気持ちで暗証番号を聞いて開けてみたが中は空っぽ。サポートの外国人風のオバサンとああでもない、こうでもないと３０分以上電話で話しながら事務所の中を探す。 そのうちファックス・マシーンの裏側に封筒が二つ落ちているのを見つける。ひとつに自分の名前を発見！ 中にカギも入っている。ポーランド系と思しきカスタマーセンターのオバサンは、Good job!と電話の向こうで笑っている。どっと疲れる体験だった。余談だが、ロストバゲッジのスーツケースが真夜中の二時半に届いた。 フロントには誰もいないので携帯電話に連絡があり、建物の入り口を開けろと言う。 延着したスーツケースは破損で真っ二つに割れていた。英国のサービスは落ちるとこまで落ちたのか。

title: Great apartment... but...
text: I recently stayed at the Go Native Monument Apartments for two nights (19 December – 21 December). When we checked in we were really pleased with the apartment which was just as described and the great service received from the reception staff. We had a great nights sleep on the first night and were looking forward to the rest of our stay. However, our second night was a different story. At around 3am on Sunday morning we were woken up by loud music from one of the neighbouring apartments. This continued for two hours until 5am at which time a large group gathered outside the door of our apartment in the corridor. They were shouting loudly to each other for around 30 minutes as well as knocking on our door and ringing our doorbell several times. As there is no manned reception in the night and only a telephone number to ring in emergencies I raised this with reception when checking out who informed me they had experienced problems with the group who were a ‘late booking’. They assured me they were going to investigate. I didn't hear anything further and received no response to my email containing these comments when asked for feedback by Go Native. Overall, the apartment and location are fantastic but our experience on this occasion was poor.

title: Terrible experience. Avoid at all costs.
text: Price seemed reasonable, perfect location, and nice pictures. Stayed for 8 nights and could not sleep at all. Being a student hall, I expected silent rooms to be able to study and rest, but I got coughing noises from the neighbor, the entrance doorbell, foot traffic by reception inside a room with a bed, desk and washbin. What they did not mention in the website at all is that windows don't shut properly, all the noise from the street comes in, as well as a nearby A/C unit which made it impossible to sleep. Staff at reception are not qualified to deal with customers or any issue outside standard check-in/check-out procedure. There is no elevator, so be sure to pack lightly or have someone carry your suitcases up the stairs..

title: Paid for QUEEN bed with sofa bed as I am 6ft8
text: Arrived at hotel went to first room with a double bed went to reception lady tried to tell me thats our queensize bed size until I got desriptions of single,double,king size and queen size beds on google had to wait 90 minutes then said can you wait until house keeping make up your room I said no were not waiting another 30-60 mins .WHat am amazed about is the MANAGER was stood at the side of her while she was struggling to give me what I had paid for and never said a word the room we was given wasnt clean the dust made me cough all nicght I have ashtma and allegic to dust I took some pictures of the walls they were filthy The sofa bed we was supposed to get wasnt in the room the beds were 2 single beds nice for a romantic night away ! The morning after I asked for the manager the person in the blue suit who was there when we checked in said I am the manager I said you was there yesterday and you did nothing to help us I said I will complain to there head office stay in holiday inns all across europe regulary this is my last stay ever at 1 of there brands .

title: Small, cheap, impersonal.
text: The hotel OneSixTwo in Westcombe Hill, Greenwich, is advertised as a “boutique hotel”, which to me gives the impression of a fashionable, cosy, and a delightfully intimate alternative to the large impersonal hotel chains

title: Misleading website and reviews
text: Cannot understand the good reviews on here. Ruined a romantic weekend. Room was tiny, noisy and dirty, up steep stairs. Bathroom tiny with peeling paint. No reception area. Looked more like a dentists from the front. Will not be returning.

title: Entry to the underworld...
text: A rare trip to London and am usually careful about where we stay. This popped up on booking.com and seemed a good price. But I didn't read trip advisor so that'll teach me... Hotel was part of a cafe on the ground floor, all looked smart and nice. Then they told us to go to level -1 so the basement beckoned. The room was clean and smart. But we have cats and couldn't have swung one... It was so small one of us had to sit on the bed out of the way for the other to move around. And the same choice of disinfectant as Virgin Train toilets was unfortunate and to be honest it was like it just masked the smell of other peoples poo. It was a smell we couldn't live with even for the limited time we planned to be there. And as we in the basement, it didn't have a window. This was not made clear when we booked or would have gone elsewhere The young woman on the desk was very helpful but couldn't move us so we left for another hotel. We appreciate that basement rooms are not uncommon in London however it would be useful to say in advance if this is what is being booked. Some people really don't like them and most people would like to know. And please change that disinfectant...!! We never did find out where the locked door in our room led to!! The ministry of magic? A Virgin train? We'll never know...

title: Not what you anticipated
text: Me and my boyfriend stayed here for 3 nights for my 21st birthday getaway in London (we've never been London before). It wasn't hard to find, after you get your head round the underground, however the hotel itself is mainly a coffee shop with some rooms to stay in. We stayed in the basement with no window, which we didn't really mind cause it's not the nicest area to be looking at. The reception is a small corner of the coffee shop. We got into our room and our kettle was missing and the website and guest book quoted we would get a hair dryer, which was also missing. So we asked to have both and the lady knocked on our door to give the items. The kettle, however, when plugged in set the electrics off. She kept asking us for a light but our phones had died so we were standing in pitch black trying to look where the electrics were (she didn't know herself). My boyfriend then remembered he had his surface on him so used that as a light. She eventually got the electrics back on but then tried the kettle again for it to go off again. There was a door next to the bed locked and I asked what was inside and the lady refused to tell us, saying that it didn't matter... well no that's just weird, you could at least tell me what is behind the door. The socket next to one side of the bed wasn't screwed in properly so therefore dangerous to use. Overall, we didn't really care as much cause we were out and about the majority of the time. On the last day, I decided I wanted a full English breakfast because I remembered seeing a poster advertising it in the coffee shop. When I asked to have one, the lady said no I had to book it because she didn't have the ingredients... I'd say try staying somewhere else, not just because the hotel itself, but the area isn't the nicest.

title: Meh...
text: The hotels pictures are misleading. The room it a lot smaller than their strategic photography! The TV didn’t work and the curtain was falling down. The one pillow might as well have not even been there and the bed is very small. At breakfast you get a different menu to the public that doesn’t have as much choice. The woman taking our order didn’t speak very good English and I ended up with a weird spinach smoothie when I asked for some apple juice which I was charged extra for!!

title: A Complete Disappointment
text: First of all, when we walked in and throughout our stay we found clumps of hair on the floor as seen in the pictures. We arrived during the extreme heat which is completely out of the Cricklewood’s Control, but they offered no fans or anything and we were on the third floor. Our room was almost 90 degrees when we checked in to the place. When we checked in and checked out was the only time the front desk was available. The shower was extremely small. I’m 5 feet and 7 inches tall and weigh 127 pounds. Every time I’d move I’d turn the water off or to hot or cold. It also took approximately 5 minutes every morning to get any hot water. Our last night we had no internet. We tried calling as that was a necessity for our family to stay in contact with family and plan the next day. Myself and daughters went down at 9:07 pm to talk to someone about the issue and of course no one was at the front desk. We rang the bell multiple times and no one answered. The next day when we checked out we actually saw someone...we asked about the internet and he said it was out of his control. A sign letting us know that there was no internet would have been helpful!!! Lastly this place is cheap...however it is also about a $15-20 Uber ride one way, to everything you will want to see and that’s only 4 Miles! So we would have been much better off paying an extra $40 a night. Please beware!!

title: Not the best
text: When checking in, the guy on reception was extremely helpful, and a lovely guy to chat to too! The room itself was the only downside to this hotel! Looking past the dated decor, it still needs a makeover! Parts of the carpet are worn down, head board falling off (wouldn’t like to think why), lack of black out curtains waking me up at an ungodly hour! Upon closer inspection, I found around the skirting boards hadn’t been cleaned thoroughly in quite some time, leaving a build up of dust... and a previous guests finger nail clipping! This hotel is in fantastic location for Wembley Stadium, however is on a busy road, with lots of traffic, causing noise through the night (which is of course no ones fault). Me and my sister in law came to see Taylor Swift, and found it was a 10 minuet walk to Kilburn Station, 4 stops, then you’re at Wembley Park Station, where you have a further 5 minuets walk to the stadium! There is a small, very tight car park at the back of the hotel, costing £10 per night, which you almost don’t have much choice other than to use it, as there are no other car parks around, and on street parking is Permit Holders only, or Pay and Display. The one star is only for the guy on reception and the location. Would only stay again if I seen they’d updated their hotel

title: Small rooms
text: Having read some of the reviews I thought this hotel would be OK as it is fairly close to Covent Garden. I wasn't prepared for how small the rooms actually are. It may be ok if you are fairly young and are used to sleeping in a cupboard but my husband and I are not. We booked a queen room expecting more room but no, the bed was under the window with only one side accessible so one of us had to clamber across to get to the other side. The en suite is part of the room so if you're sharing a room make sure you know them very well! On the positive side, there is free wifi, soft towels, tea and coffee, and the room is clean. I won't be staying there again.
